articles.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Work to restore the terminus was started in 2022
After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali.

Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter.

Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.

Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.

Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days.

Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter.

Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality.

Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri.

Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days.

Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus.

articles.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs
Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday.
The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town.

Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects.

They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them.

The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way.

articles.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences

A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently.

The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai.

Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot.

Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized.

The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences. They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary. A case was registered and a probe is under way.

articles.title: T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the combined storage was around 92%
Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time, if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue.

As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

The State’s largest dam, Mettur, has about 23 thousand million cubic feet (tmcft) but this is hardly enough for the authorities to maintain sustained release of water to farmers, beyond a week, in the Cauvery delta.

The rainfall during the Northeast monsoon has been moderate as the State has received around 240 mm of rainfall against the anticipated 236 mm. It should get at least 260 mm more to be considered comfortable, the most of which should materialise in November. Ordinarily, December yields only about 20% of the total rainfall of the monsoon.

In fact, the existing pattern of rainfall registered by the State so far during the season appears to be more in tune with the forecast made by the Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), which, in late September, predicted that the State would get 438 mm during the entire monsoon against the normal 434 mm, a deviation of one per cent. The Meteorological department, in its outlook at the beginning of October for the season, referred to the southern peninsular region of the country in general and stated that the expected rainfall “ is most likely to be normal (88-112%) of the Long Period Average (LPA).”

The TNAU, which was more specific in its forecast than the Meteorological department, had anticipated only a normal rainfall for the core districts of the Cauvery delta – Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai. Despite the water availability at Mettur not being comfortable and the expectation of a subdued rainfall, farmers have gone in for raising paddy during the samba-thaladi cultivation season to the tune of around 3.62 lakh hectares. Of this, nearly 50% falls under “direct sown“ category of cultivation, which means that seeds are directly sown instead of transplantation. This method is followed in times of water shortage.

But, the problem with water availability seems to be higher in the remaining areas of the State, a reflection of which can be seen in the way the farmers have taken to paddy this time. The paddy coverage in the non-delta areas of the State is about 1.3 lakh hectares shorter than what it was last year. As compared to the previous year’s share (39%) of direct sowing in the overall paddy coverage, this time the method’s share is about 57%. In 2025-26, rice production in the State was 77.5 lakh tonnes, about one lakh tonnes lower than the previous high of 79.07 lakh tonnes during 2021-22.

As part of its efforts for protecting the crop in the Cauvery delta, the State government, at meetings of the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) on Friday, demanded that Karnataka release around 20. 7 tmcft including the backlog of about 16.9 tmc ft. However, the Authority ratified the decision of the Committee, which had recommended that Karnataka release 3.88 tmcft to Tamil Nadu through 3,000 cubic feet per second (cusecs) per day for 15 days from Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: Sustainable Development Council unveils nationwide citizen driven initiative for sustainable India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sustainable Development Council (SDC), an international non-profit organisation holding Special Consultative Status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), unveiled MyBharat2030, a nationwide citizen-driven survey initiative at the 2nd World Cities Day Connect 2026 in Chennai recently.

According to a press release, MyBharat2030 seeks to understand people’s aspirations, capture their perspectives and assess collective progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The initiative marks a significant step towards strengthening citizen engagement in India’s journey towards a progressive, inclusive and sustainable future.

The initiative was inaugurated in the presence of P. Venkataramanan, Minister for Food and Civil Supplies; B. Rajkumar, Minister for Housing and Urban Development, and Sowmiya Anbumani, MLA and president of the PMK’s Pasumai Thayagam. Amudhavalli Ranganathan, Chairperson (India), Sustainable Development Council; Datchanamoorthy Ramu, founder-president; and Gokulnath Mathiyazhagan, secretary-general were among those present on the occasion.

articles.title: PM Modi to celebrate Deepavali with forces in Bastar that was once den of Maoists
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will celebrate Deepavali on Sunday (November 8, 2026) along with security personnel in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, which was freed from the clutches of Maoists after several decades.
"Heading to Bastar to celebrate Diwali with our brave security forces," Mr. Modi said in a post on 'X'.
The Prime Minister said Bastar is an area where Maoism once held sway but now, development is flourishing.
"I am going to salute our brave security personnel for their sacrifices, selfless service and unwavering devotion to the nation," he said.
The Central Armed Police Forces and personnel of the Chhattisgarh Police have been deployed in Bastar. They were deeply involved in the anti-Maoist operations.
On March 31 this year, the government had announced that the country was free from the menace of Maoism after the elimination of many leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.

While conveying Deepavali greetings on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the Prime Minister said that like the previous year, this time also, he would celebrate the festival along with the brave soldiers of the country.
In a video message posted on his social media handles, Mr. Modi had said that like everyone, he will also celebrate Deepavali with great enthusiasm.
"My heartiest greetings to all of you for Deepavali. I wish for peace, prosperity and happiness for all of you in the coming days. I also celebrate Deepavali like you with great enthusiasm," he said.
The Prime Minister said everyone knows that every year he celebrates Deepavali with the brave soldiers of the country.
"This time also I will continue the tradition," he said.

articles.title: Rajnath Singh pays tributes to brave soldiers at Sherethang in Sikkim
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday (November 8, 2026) visited Sherethang near Nathu La in Sikkim, where he paid homage to brave soldiers at a war memorial.

He was received at Sherethang by Gangtok District Collector Rohan Agawane, Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Tsering Namgyal Gyatso and Home Department's Joint Secretary John Gurung along with senior army officials.

Mr. Singh paid homage at the Sherethang War Memorial in East Sikkim, honouring the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the service of the nation and paid tribute to their courage and valour in safeguarding the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, officials said.
The Minister interacted with defence personnel deployed in the region and hailed their dedication and service in protecting the country's borders under challenging conditions, they said.
Mr. Singh also visited Baba Harbhajan Singh Mandir and paid his respects at the revered shrine, which holds immense significance among army personnel.

Punjab Police, with the support of central agencies, has secured the deportation of wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia following a 10-month international manhunt.
Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹5 lakh for information leading to his arrest.

"In a major breakthrough, Anti-Gangster Task Force (#AGTF) Punjab, in coordination with the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (#OFTEC) of Counter Intelligence, Punjab with the support of central agencies, secures the deportation of Gurwinder alias Afridi, a key kingpin of the Doni Bal-Prabh Dassuwal gang, from Ethiopia following a 10-month-long international manhunt under Operation SHAHID," the DGP said in a post on X.

Preliminary investigation reveals that the accused was allegedly directing targeted killings, extortion-related firing incidents and organised criminal activities in Punjab from abroad. articles.title: BJP celebrates Advani’s birthday with puja, havan; leaders laud his role in Indian politics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The event, coinciding with Deepavali, was organised to commemorate Mr. Advani’s life, dedication to the nation, organisational contributions and long public career, the BJP said

The BJP on Sunday (November 8, 2026) celebrated the 99th birthday of party veteran and former deputy Prime Minister Lal Krishna Advani with a puja and havan at its headquarters here, while several leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, lauded his contributions to Indian politics.
The event, coinciding with Deepavali, was organised to commemorate Mr. Advani’s life, dedication to the nation, organisational contributions and long public career, the BJP said.
Several party leaders, including Mr. Advani’s daughter Pratibha Advani and BJP president Nitin Nabin, attended the event.

The puja and havan were followed by the screening of a 20-minute video highlighting key speeches and episodes from Mr. Advani’s life. Presentations featuring addresses by senior leaders reflecting on his contributions and significant moments in his political journey were also held.

In an authored article, Mr. Modi said two qualities that set the BJP patriarch apart were his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness, besides his ability to expose what he described as the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity.
Mr. Modi also said Mr. Advani and former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee set a remarkable example of cooperation and together changed the course of Indian politics.

In a post on X, Mr. Nabin described Mr. Advani as a guide for all and credited him with making an unforgettable contribution to the expansion of the organisation, from the Jana Sangh to the BJP, taking nationalist ideology to every citizen and turning the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi movement into a mass movement.
“Your integrity in public life and unwavering commitment to the organisation will always be a source of inspiration for all BJP workers,” Mr. Nabin said.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah described Mr. Advani as “a symbol of service to the nation, an architect of the BJP and a principled statesman”.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Advani had set new standards of integrity, dedication and leadership throughout his public life.
Senior BJP leader and Union Minister Piyush Goyal described him as “an extraordinary example of loyalty to the nation, steadfastness in his convictions, and dedication to the organisation”.

articles.title: Trump offers UFC boss press secretary post, urges criminal probes of Democrats
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Dana White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”

Facing an incoming Democratic Congress, U.S. President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday (November 7, 2026), offering friend and “violent fighter” Dana White the White House press secretary job and ordering the Justice Department to investigate his opponents.

Democrats handed Mr. Trump’s Republicans a blowout defeat in the midterm elections this week and will take control of both chambers of Congress in January. They promise robust investigations into Mr. Trump and his administration.
Mr. Trump, however, showed no signs of being chastened.
He offered the press secretary post to Mr. White, a loyal supporter and head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts organisation.
“Dana, please take the job!” Mr. Trump posted on social media, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior.”

Speaking to reporters following a boxing event in London late Saturday (November 7, 2026), Mr. White said he was flying to Washington “right now” and will meet with Mr. Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026).
Mr. White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”
Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”
“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”
Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”
Saturday’s (November 7, 2026) announcements came a day after Mr. Trump appointed Stephen Miller to be his next chief of staff, describing the combative senior adviser as “a great fighter.”
He replaces Susie Wiles, whose departure marks the first staffing fallout from the Republican election debacle.

articles.title: Strong earthquake shakes central Japan, shattering store windows, injuring at least 22
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometres below the earth’s surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions

“Please be on the lookout for mudslides, falling rocks and the possible effects from rainfall,” Ayataka Ebita, an agency official, told reporters.
He said no apparent change was detected so far to the Nankai Trough plate, where scientists say a megaquake can possibly hit.
The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

articles.title: Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament

Israel’s president on Saturday (November 7, 2026) chose Gadi Eisenkot , Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try ‌to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with ​a clear path to power.

Mr. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in ⁠office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he ‌would have a majority of seats in parliament. But Arab leaders, incensed by what they view as the racist policies of Mr. Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Mr. Eisenkot ‌to try to form a government first — giving him the most endorsements.

“President Herzog has invited ‌Gadi ⁠Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow,” ⁠said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections.
Weeks of protracted negotiations are expected to follow Mr. Eisenkot’s nomination. He has 28 days ​to try to forge a government, with a ‌possible 14-day extension.

His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Mr. Netanyahu.

Analysts say that all three options ‌are unlikely to take shape. If Mr. Eisenkot fails, another candidate can try to form ​a government and if that candidate fails, parliament can nominate another. There is a deadline for the process of around 100 days. If no one succeeds, another election ⁠is held.
Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Mr. Netanyahu’s wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority.

Mr. Eisenkot’s Yashar party emerged as ‌the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel’s Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats.
A son of Moroccan immigrants, Mr. Eisenkot, 66, would be the country’s first Prime Minister from Israel’s Mizrahi community, Jews who trace their roots to West Asia and North Africa.

Reserved and media-shy, Mr. Eisenkot only entered politics in 2022. He briefly served in Mr. Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet following Hamas’ October 7, 2023, attack ‌on Israel before returning to the opposition.
From opposition, he publicly rebuked Mr. Netanyahu over his leadership, including his management of the ​military campaign in Gaza, and has sworn that he would not serve in government with him.

articles.title: Iran says two tankers caught fire in Hormuz after hitting mines
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic
Two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Sunday (November 8, 2026), according to state news agency IRNA .
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

"Two oil tankers violating regulations — one in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the strait — caught fire and are currently engulfed in intense flames after striking naval mines while attempting to cross through unauthorised routes," the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said in a statement.

"The two tankers had reportedly committed multiple violations, including switching off their navigation and positioning systems, as they attempted to transit through an unauthorised route," the statement added.
The Guards did not specify the name or nationality of the tankers.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.
The IRNA separately reported late on Saturday (November 7) that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.
"Sounds resembling explosions were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas. The cause of the sounds remains unknown," the news agency wrote on Telegram.
Officials confirmed an "impact" in the port city of Jask, the IRNA said.
U.S. President Donald Trump previously talked up the possibility of resuming heavy strikes on Iran but has since walked back from the idea.

articles.title: Body of Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota brought to Mansa for last rites
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13
The mortal remains of s lain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder last month triggered protests and a political row, were brought to his native place here on Sunday for last rites.
Following a post-mortem at PGIMER in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Jhota's body was taken to his native place, where last rites would be conducted.

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A large number of people turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
On Saturday (November 7, 2026), a member of the joint action committee had said Jhota's cremation would take place at his native place in Mansa on Sunday.
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota's murder.
The cremation will be held at Jhota's fields on Chakerian Road in Mansa. Jhota's father, Bhim Singh, on Saturday (November 7, 2026) called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse.

"We will take the body to our residence first and thereafter, between 12 and 1 pm, Jhota will be cremated on Diwali Day," said Singh while speaking to reporters in Chandigarh on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Jhota's body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday, after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), Jhota's father said he would go on a fast demanding the immediate transfer of Mansa Senior Superintendent of Police Vaibhav Chaudhary.

Jhota's family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist. On October 28, two JAC members, Lakhvir Singh and Mohanjit Singh Sheron, were arrested during the protest.

On the evening of November 5, the JAC members were released from Nabha district jail after a meeting between the protesters and government representatives, including Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, on November 4.

articles.title: Thane court sentences man to 20 years rigorous imprisonment for raping minor on promise of marriage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused
A special court in Maharashtra's Thane district has sentenced a 35-year-old man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for repeatedly raping a minor girl after promising to marry her.

Additional Sessions Judge Premal S. Vithalani convicted the accused, Shrinivas Ashok Yelgonda, a painter, under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, noting that while the absence of violence and premeditation was a mitigating factor, the law mandated a minimum 20-year term.

According to the prosecution, the victim resided in the same housing society in Diva East as the accused, and the two became acquainted in June 2020 and subsequently developed a romantic relationship through phone chats.

Special public prosecutor Rekha Hiwrale stated that the accused first sexually assaulted the minor in November 2020 inside a neighbour's vacant apartment by promising to marry her, and later raped her on several occasions. The abuse came to light in February 2022 when a dispute arose after the accused reneged on his promise to marry her.
Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused.

The defence argued that there was an unexplained delay in registering the FIR in 2022, and that exact dates of the recurring assaults were missing. However, relying on the survivor's birth certificate and school leaving certificate, the court verified that she was a "child" under 18 years of age during the major part of the abuse timeline, rendering her legal consent immaterial.

"The evidence on record clearly establishes that the victim was under the bona fide impression that the accused would solemnise marriage with her, which led her to keep the relationship and the repeated physical intimacies concealed from her parents," the judge observed.
The subsequent deliberation by the family before approaching the police is both natural and understandable given the social stigma, honour, and future of an unmarried girl, the court said.
It also noted that there was no evidence of brutal force, physical injury or premeditated sexual predation.

"While the victim's minority under the age of 18 renders her consent legally ineffective and makes the conviction unavoidable, the romantic backdrop remains a vital and compelling mitigating factor in sentencing," it stated.
The court sentenced the convict to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹5,000.

Vithalani convicted the accused, Shrinivas Ashok Yelgonda, a painter, under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, noting that while the absence of violence and premeditation was a mitigating factor, the law mandated a minimum 20-year term.

According to the prosecution, the victim resided in the same housing society in Diva East as the accused, and the two became acquainted in June 2020 and subsequently developed a romantic relationship through phone chats.

Special public prosecutor Rekha Hiwrale stated that the accused first sexually assaulted the minor in November 2020 inside a neighbour's vacant apartment by promising to marry her, and later raped her on several occasions. The abuse came to light in February 2022 when a dispute arose after the accused reneged on his promise to marry her.

Four prosecution witnesses, including the survivor, her mother and neighbour, were examined to prove the charges against the accused.

The defence argued that there was an unexplained delay in registering the FIR in 2022, and that exact dates of the recurring assaults were missing. However, relying on the survivor's birth certificate and school leaving certificate, the court verified that she was a "child" under 18 years of age during the major part of the abuse timeline, rendering her legal consent immaterial.

"The evidence on record clearly establishes that the victim was under the bona fide impression that the accused would solemnise marriage with her, which led her to keep the relationship and the repeated physical intimacies concealed from her parents," the judge observed.

The subsequent deliberation by the family before approaching the police is both natural and understandable given the social stigma, honour, and future of an unmarried girl, the court said.

It also noted that there was no evidence of brutal force, physical injury or premeditated sexual predation.

"While the victim's minority under the age of 18 renders her consent legally ineffective and makes the conviction unavoidable, the romantic backdrop remains a vital and compelling mitigating factor in sentencing," it stated.

The court sentenced the convict to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹5,000.

articles.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the Election Commission of India

The Congress party's receipts from donations above ₹20,000 plunged nearly 75% to ₹130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows.
The party had received ₹517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.
A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86% from ₹141.46 crore the previous year.

The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received ₹281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to ₹517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held.

BJP received ₹6,074.02 crore in donations exceeding ₹20,000 in 2024-25, nearly 12 times Congress's collection. BJP's corresponding figure for 2025-26 is not available as the party's contribution report has not been made public by the ECI yet.
The BJP collected more than the Congress in each of the 12 financial years examined.

Funding through Prudent Electoral Trust accounted for a substantial part of Congress' latest decline. The trust's contribution fell from ₹216.34 crore in 2024-25 to ₹25 crore in 2025-26, a drop of about 88%.
Prudent was the only electoral trust listed in the party's latest contribution report.
Among other large contributors were Star Cement, which gave ₹5 crore, Sajjan Bhajanka, who contributed ₹4 crore, and Prem Kumar Bhajanka, who donated ₹2 crore.
The Congress' 2025-26 fund collection, though sharply lower than the previous year, was not its lowest over the period examined.
Its disclosed donations were lower in several earlier years, including ₹74.52 crore in 2020-21, ₹95.46 crore in 2021-22 and ₹79.92 crore in 2022-23.

These figures exclude electoral bonds, which were reported separately when the scheme operated. Including bond receipts in the earlier years, the Congress' latest collection in 2025-26 was its lowest since 2020-21.

articles.title: Dangerous harmonies: Is there a hidden villain in India’s devastating electrical fires?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electrical causes are predominating in India’s recent fire incidents; while codes and guidelines are covering these increasingly, there are still major gaps such as taking into account harmonic currents put into the system by state-of-the-art electronics equipment
Just after 3.48 a.m. on May 3, 2026, fire ripped through a four-storey building in Vivek Vihar, East Delhi, killing nine. The suspected origin was an AC blast or short circuit.

Ten newborns died in an overcrowded Jhansi NICU in November 2024, a unit meant for 18 babies packed with 55. Three newborns in Amravati this August, dead not from flame but from smoke inhalation, even though the fire itself was out within 30 minutes. One newborn in Chhindwara two days before that. Ten patients at Cuttack’s SCB Medical College this March, when a short circuit in a trauma-ICU air-conditioner ignited an oxygen-rich ward at 3 a.m.

Fire accidents in India used to happen in industrial units, firecracker factories and mass gatherings. No more. The more devastating ones happen right in our neighbourhoods, in hospitals and high-rises. They are almost always triggered by electrical fires.

Delhi Fire Service attributes over 80% of the capital’s fires to electrical faults. Mumbai Fire Brigade, analysing 26,855 incidents over five years, attributes nearly three in four to the same cause. New Delhi alone saw a 37% rise in residential fires this year over last, with roughly 70% traced to short-circuiting, faulty wiring, overheating, and overloaded circuits. The National Crime Records Bureau recorded 7,566 fire accidents and 7,435 deaths in 2022, with short circuit consistently among the largest single causes.

Indian electricity demand hit 256.11 GW on April 25 this year, against air temperatures of 47 degrees, roughly double the early-2010s peak. A/Cs draw about 50 GW at peak. And projections place the A/C load at 180 GW in another 10 years. Indians bought more than 15 million air-conditioners in 2025 alone, and the International Energy Agency expects the installed base to climb from 93 million units in 2024 to 240 million by 2030.

Air-conditioners draw heavy current that electrical systems in older buildings are unable to withstand, resulting in the wiring burning up. What’s called an A/C blast is the overworked compressor in the refrigeration exploding due to sheer heat caused by overworking. Investigation into these fires has been hampered by shortage of certified fire forensic investigators. Too often, the causes are dismissed as blasts or short circuits. Root cause analysis and systemic remedies are rarely formulated.

An electrical circuit has three parts. The load is whatever draws current. It could be just a light or an air-conditioner. The wiring carries that current, insulated to keep two conductors from touching. The protection device, typically a miniature circuit breaker, is meant to cut the current flow the instant something goes wrong. The circuit breaker switches off the current within about a tenth of a second for a short circuit, or within a longer window, from a minute to an hour, for a sustained overload. A fire needs two failures at once: something in the load or wiring goes wrong, and the protection device fails to trip in time.

A peer-reviewed 2025 review in the journal Fire identifies six recurring failure modes behind that first failure: short circuits, overloads, loose or oxidised connections, series and parallel arc faults, ground faults, and equipment ageing. Of these, a loose connection is often the quietest killer. Research on wiring practice, cited in Indian engineering literature reviewing fire risk in electrical installations, shows that loose terminal connections, whether from bad workmanship, thermal expansion and contraction, or simple ageing, create a phenomenon called glowing contact: a slow-building hot spot that can smoulder in a wall or panel for months before anything is visible from outside.

There is a second, slower mechanism that gets far less attention and could explain a great deal about how India’s fires happen: harmonics. Every inverter-driven air-conditioner, along with every UPS, LED driver, ventilator and EV charger, draws current in short, jagged pulses rather than a smooth wave. This injects distortion into the electrical supply at multiples of the base 50 Hz frequency. In three-phase buildings, certain harmonic orders, called triplen harmonics, do not cancel out in the neutral conductor the way normal, balanced current does. Instead they add up. The neutral wire, which was never designed to be load-bearing and carries no circuit breaker of its own, quietly overheats. A loose joint nearby could make an overheated neutral become an ignition source ripping up ordinary insulation.

Fire investigators suspect that many chemicals and solvents are used in ICUs and the vapours they generate don’t get evacuated well-known enough because of poor maintenance of ventilation systems. They point out that ICUs have dedicated ventilation systems and need much care. While these vapours provide the fuel, a source of heat is required for ignition. And that is where harmonics-generated heating could come into play, says a fire forensic engineer who didn’t wish to be named. “Electrical fires are a gray area and require a lot of precautions. Sadly, in India, compliance with regulations is considered a financial burden,” he adds.

Medical equipment damaged after a fire broke out in the neonatal intensive care unit of a government hospital killing three newborns, in Amravati district of Maharashtra. | Photo Credit: EMMANUAL YOGINI

Among the first cases of a spectacular failure due to harmonics happened in September 2010, when a capacitor inside a harmonic filter aboard the cruise liner Queen Mary 2 failed while the ship approached Barcelona with 3,823 people aboard. The explosion blacked out the vessel.

articles.title: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused fired several rounds at the victim and his son; the victim succumbed to injuries and the son escaped unhurt

A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.
The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.

An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.

“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.

A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

articles.title: Sanskrit University suspension row: Govindan backs stir, says it should go on till suspended students write exams
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sixteen students were suspended after a Students’ Federation of India-led protest during a syndicate meeting on August 13 over a lack of adequate campus facilities

CPI(M) state secretary M.V. Govindan on Sunday (November 8, 2026) expressed solidarity with the ongoing agitation by students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit at Kalady near Kochi, saying the protest should continue until all the suspended students are allowed to appear for their examinations.
Sixteen students were suspended after a Students’ Federation of India (SFI)-led protest during a syndicate meeting on August 13 over a lack of adequate campus facilities.
They were accused of staging a “mock cremation” of Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas, manhandling her and attempting to damage university property.

A single bench of the Kerala High Court had directed the university to allow the students to appear for the examinations, but a division bench later stayed the order . The students then approached the Supreme Court, which directed the single bench to decide the matter.

In a Facebook post after visiting the protest tent and interacting with the students, Mr. Govindan said the agitation would not be called off merely with an apology.

articles.title: Conservative activists storm Deepavali celebrations in Seattle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Conservative activists led by Jake Lang stormed Deepavali celebrations in Seattle carrying placards calling for deporting all “dot heads”, an act that was swiftly condemned by U.S. lawmakers and community leaders.

Mr. Lang and fellow activist Thomas Allen waved the American flag and carried placards with slogans “Deport All Dot Heads" and "Stop Hindu Replacement of Christians” in front of a stage where a dance performance was being held on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Videos of the storming of the Deepavali celebrations in Seattle went viral on social media.

The activists were soon escorted out of the Deepavali celebrations at the Seattle Center Armoury which was part of Seattle Center Festal, a series of 25 free cultural festivals that collectively draw about 400,000 visitors annually.

Mr. Lang is associated with an organisation ‘White Replacement’ and was among the attackers of the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021. He served a four-year jail term and was later pardoned by US President Donald Trump on the first day of his second presidency in 2025
Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal said she was "beyond disgusted” at the vile and racist display.

“I am beyond disgusted by this vile and racist display. Diwali is an important holiday and our community should feel safe to celebrate it. This hateful display has no place in our city or this country,” Ms. Jayapal, the Congresswoman from Washington, said in a post on X.
Former White House advisor Ajay Jain Bhutoria said the actions of Lang and Allen were “absolutely disgusting.”

“Targeting Hindu Americans and Indian immigrants with racial slurs and conspiracy rhetoric has no place in this country. We stand against this racism and for the right of every American to celebrate their heritage freely,” Mr. Bhutoria said in a post on X.

“We condemn such actions and advise community members to stay vigilant while celebrating Diwali, as these activists have announced plans to disrupt other celebrations,” Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) said in a post on X.

Sunita Vishwanath, co-founder of Hindus for Human Rights, said anti-immigrant sentiment has taken the form of anti-Hindu hatred extreme enough for Christian xenophobes to "storm" a Deepavali celebration in Seattle with signs like, "Deport all Dotheads."

“This is as heartbreaking as the Hindutva mobs that harass Christians in India on Christmas, forcing church congregations to say 'Jai Shri Ram' at the threat of violence,” Ms. Vishwanath said in a post on X.

articles.title: Nithya Raman | The urban planner
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Before entering U.S. politics, L.A.’s first South Asian Mayor-elect worked among the urban poor in Chennai, where she used data to expose gaps in slum resettlement and public facilities

After defeating Karen Bass, the incumbent Mayor of the second most populous city of the U.S., Nithya Raman wrote on X, “Los Angeles, I am deeply honored to be your next mayor.” A member of the city council since 2020, Ms. Raman has a track record of civic activism, advocating for affordable and increased housing. Entering the electoral race at the very last minute, she is now L.A.’s the first South Asian Mayor-elect as well as the first candidate to defeat an incumbent Mayor of the city since 2005.

Born in Keralam, Ms. Raman spent a part of her early childhood between Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur. Her father, Venkataraman, used to work for Keltron, and her mother, Sudha, was a former employee of the Indian Overseas Bank. The family migrated to the U.S. when Ms. Raman was six. She graduated from Harvard University in 2003, and then got a master’s degree in urban planning from MIT. She became a U.S. citizen at 22.

articles.title: Jon Ossoff | Ambition without ambition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While headlines scream Ossoff looks more presidential after his Senate win, he remains focused on his State while attacking Donald Trump and his family

There is something of an investigative journalist in Jon Ossoff, who served as managing director and chief executive officer of Insight: The World Investigates, a London-based investigative television production company. During his Senate campaign as Democratic candidate in Georgia and even before, he had been mounting a blistering campaign against corruption. It resonated with the voters struggling with rising food prices and unaffordable fuel.

Mr. Ossoff won the November 3 election against Republican Mike Collins, becoming the only incumbent Senate Democrat to defend a seat in a State President Donald Trump carried in 2024. Ever since his win in the 2021 Senate race in Georgia, the charismatic Mr. Ossoff has been making the lists of possible candidates for the Democratic ticket in the 2028 Presidential election. But, like Barack Obama before his 2004 Senate win and scores of others before him, Mr. Ossoff, now 39, who in 2021 became the youngest U.S. Senator since 1980, has been vehemently denying any such aspiration. The media, however, has been quick in spotting in him similarities with Mr. Obama, especially the former President’s speech delivery.

articles.title: Kremlin hopes U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Republicans' defeat in the U.S. midterm elections was watched closely in Russia, where some observers are predicting it could herald more support for Ukraine when the Democrats take over Congress in January.
But if the Kremlin is hearing the ticking of a clock on its nearly 5-year-old full-scale invasion of its neighbour, it seemingly remains unperturbed.

Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that U.S. President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

“There is groundwork already in place, and another round of trilateral negotiations is set to take place very soon,” Mr. Peskov said of talks planned for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11) involving Russian, Ukrainian and U.S. representatives in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
He also praised the “successful humanitarian peace-building efforts” by first lady Melania Trump, adding that “we hope that all of this will continue.”
Last week's limited ceasefire around the Russia-occupied city of Oleshky, brokered with her help, allowed for the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of some residents.
Mr. Peskov shrugged off a question from reporters on whether the new Congress would challenge Mr. Trump's stance on Russia and Ukraine. He called it an “internal matter” for the U.S.
In recent months, Mr. Trump's actions appeared to favour Moscow

Last month, he struck a diesel fuel import deal with Russia in a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on the Kremlin, to the dismay of Ukraine and its European allies. He also claimed that Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil refineries caused a spike in diesel prices in the U.S. He urged Kyiv to halt the strikes, even though rising global energy prices were largely driven by the Iran war.

Mr. Trump also issued an executive order to put on hold sweeping new sanctions that clamped down on the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the national interest. Lawmakers from both parties blasted Mr. Trump's move as benefiting Russian President Vladimir Putin.

At the same time, Ukraine reported a throttling of Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX. Mr. Trump denied being behind the brief slowing of Starshield, but the move to limit the system that serves as the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and battlefield communications was widely seen as part of Washington's efforts to pressure Kyiv.

The diesel deal appeared to falter this week after U.S. federal and state officials warned that handling any shipments could bring legal consequences, and two U.S.-bound tankers changed course. The Kremlin sought to play down the development, saying deliveries will continue.

articles.title: New Zealanders won’t know for weeks who won election as neither side secures clear victory
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon’s centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins

New Zealanders will wait for weeks to discover who will lead the country after Saturday's (November 7, 2026) election failed to deliver a decisive win for the right or the left, leaving fraught negotiations for a wafer-thin governing majority the only apparent path to victory for either side.

The tightest vote in years delivered a stinging rebuke to the major parties which have long dominated New Zealand politics, Christopher Luxon's centre-right National party and centre-left Labour led by Chris Hipkins, as voters threw more support behind minor parties on the ideological flanks than before.
On Saturday's (November 7) numbers, minor parties would enter negotiations for a governing deal with leverage to extract deeper policy concessions from a weakened National or Labour.

The near-deadlock was partly produced because voters, apparently weary of New Zealand's economic woes and apathetic about both Luxon and Hipkins, chose to propel a new entrant group to Parliament for the first time in years.
Opportunity, led by 38-year-old business consultant and political newcomer Qiulae Wong, is unaligned with either bloc and Ms. Wong has said she could work with either side to form a government.

Ms. Wong's pledges of evidence-based centrism and an end to partisan bickering had on Saturday's (November 7) results secured seven seats for Opportunity — enough to frustrate both left and right in a simple path to power.
It was a staggering ascension for a party that made three failed attempts at Parliament before Ms. Wong became leader less than a year ago.

Other winners were harder to identify and on Sunday (November 8), “who won the election 2026” was the top trending Google search in New Zealand. So unclear was the result that parties won't begin negotiations to form a government until final tallies are released on November 27, confirming the exact number of seats they've won.

With 2.8 million ballots counted on election night, the conservative incumbent government led by Luxon's National party appeared close to the slimmest possible return to power — by just one seat. However, Mr. Luxon didn't claim victory, instead striking a note of cautious optimism that he could negotiate a second term in power.

Speaking to reporters Sunday (November 8), Luxon blamed public dissatisfaction on global shocks which have buffeted New Zealand's trade-based economy, noting that other incumbent governments worldwide have faced voters' rancor over living costs.

Yet his opponent Mr. Hipkins, who was turfed from office in 2023 largely over discontent about the same economic issues, didn't appear to benefit on Saturday. The left-wing bloc appeared to fall short of a majority but was still hopeful it could triumph — though that seemed a more remote prospect.
Electoral officials were due on Sunday (November 8) to begin counting nearly 400,000 so-called special votes, including from New Zealanders who live abroad, a process expected to take three weeks.

articles.title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution and democracy: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

“These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

articles.title: Banner seeking info on four wanted terrorists surfaces in Srinagar's Lal Chowk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A flex banner was found hanging early in the morning on the wall of Pratap Park in Srinagar, seeking information about the four terrorists, including Mohammad Lateef Bhat, involved in the killing of a cop in Anantnag in July this year
A banner seeking information about the whereabouts of four terrorists wanted by security forces surfaced on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in Srinagar's Lal Chowk area.

A flex banner was found hanging early in the morning on the wall of Pratap Park in Srinagar, seeking information about the four terrorists, including Mohammad Lateef Bhat, involved in the killing of a cop in Anantnag in July this year.
The others include Bilal Ahmad Mir, Mohammad Umar Mir and Abid Qayoom Lone, all from Baramulla district.

While Bhat, a resident of Kulgam district in south Kashmir, is active in the Kashmir Valley, the other three terrorists are currently believed to be operating from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), officials said in Srinagar.

"Anyone who can provide credible information regarding the movement/presence of these terrorists, the identity of the informant will be kept strictly confidential and a handsome reward will be given for reliable information," the banner reads.

articles.title: 'Notebandi' devastated economy, 'votebandi' destroying polity: Congress slams PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On this day in 2016, Prime Minister Modi addressed the nation and announced demonetisation of high-value currency notes of ₹500 and ₹1,000
"Notebandi" devastated the economy and "votebandi" is destroying the polity, the Congress said on Sunday (November 8, 2026), adding that both are contributions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared the screenshot of a media report which claimed that demonetisation was a disaster in 2016 and is a resounding failure 10 years on.
In his post, Mr. Ramesh said, "Notebandi devastated the economy. Votebandi is destroying the polity. Both are the contributions of the PM."
On this day in 2016, Prime Minister Modi addressed the nation and announced demonetisation of high-value currency notes of ₹500 and ₹1,000.

The Congress has consistently attacked the Narendra Modi government on every anniversary of demonetisation, saying the "reckless" decision broke the back of the Indian economy and the country will not forgive the prime minister for this "monumental disaster".
In the past, the opposition party has called demonetisation a "monumental blunder" that failed to achieve any of the "shifting goalposts" that the Modi government had proposed as objectives.

articles.title: J&K: 4 police personnel, including SHO, injured as bus rams police vehicle in Ramban
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accident occurred shortly after the police vehicle joined the escort of BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly Sunil Sharma as his convoy entered Chanderkote jurisdiction

Four police personnel, including a Station House Officer (SHO), sustained minor injuries after their vehicle overturned when it was hit by a bus on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway near Chanderkote in Ramban district on Sunday (November 8, 2026), officials said.

The accident occurred shortly after the police vehicle joined the escort of BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly Sunil Sharma as his convoy entered Chanderkote jurisdiction while travelling from Srinagar to Jammu, the officials said.

The bus hit the police vehicle at a crossing, causing it to overturn on the highway. Four police personnel, including the SHO Inspector Vicky Thapa were injured in the incident. They were taken to District Hospital Ramban for treatment, officials said.
Mr. Sharma, who stopped his convoy and joined the rescue efforts after witnessing the accident, said the police vehicle suffered extensive damage, but all personnel on board were safe.

“Vehicles travel at high speeds on national highways, and failure to exercise caution while approaching crossings can lead to such accidents. The manner in which the bus hit the police vehicle underscores the need for greater vigilance at crossings, particularly those along national highways,” he told PTI .
Medical Superintendent of District Hospital Ramban, Dr. Mohammad Rafi Wani, said the condition of the four police personnel was stable.

Four police personnel, including a Station House Officer (SHO), sustained minor injuries after their vehicle overturned when it was hit by a bus on the Jammu-Srinagar National Highway near Chanderkote in Ramban district on Sunday (November 8, 2026), officials said.

“Vehicles travel at high speeds on national highways, and failure to exercise caution while approaching crossings can lead to such accidents. Medical Superintendent of District Hospital Ramban, Dr. Mohammad Rafi Wani, said the condition of the four police personnel was stable.

"After receiving first aid and undergoing necessary scans, the injured policemen were discharged," he said.

articles.title: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy alleges Hassan DC retained her post by paying bribe district minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy has alleged that the Hassan Deputy Commissioner retained her post by paying ₹75 lakh to Excise Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also the in-charge Minister of Hassan district.

Speaking to presspersons in Hassan after visiting the historic Hasanamba temple in Hassan on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Kumaraswamy read out excerpts from a written script of what he described as a WhatsApp conversation between an unidentified person and Shashikiran, the personal assistant to the Hassan Deputy Commissioner. He said he received the contents of the conversation from an official who met him the previous night.

According to Mr. Kumaraswamy, the conversation was about seeking permission for three stone crushers. The personal assistant allegedly demanded ₹60 lakh to get the clearance. As the person on the other end bargained, Mr. Shashikiran is said to have listed the people with whom the amount had to be shared.

Mr. Kumaraswamy said the conversation also mentioned that Mr. Shivalinge Gowda wanted to transfer the incumbent Deputy Commissioner from Hassan. However, she allegedly managed to convince the Minister by paying ₹75 lakh through Arsikere Tahsildar Santosh.
The script of the purported conversation was also distributed to journalists. Mr. Kumaraswamy said it also referred to the Hassan MP and several officials of the district.
He demanded an investigation into the allegations and urged the police to seize the mobile phone from the person concerned for further examination.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who also visited the temple the same day, said the Deputy Commissioner had been doing a good job. “However, allegations are being made against her because she did not yield to their demands,” he said.

Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal. “I have not done anything wrong, I am not doing anything wrong, and I will never do anything wrong,” she said.

Ms. Kumari said that if any wrong message had been sent by her personal assistant or anyone in his section, proper action would be taken. She condemned the circulation of “false and baseless information”. “Let there be an inquiry. Those who have erred should face action,” she said.
She said a complaint would be filed with the cyber police, as spreading false information was a crime. “We will bring out the truth,” she added.

articles.title: No concrete proof yet from Indonesia for claim over rescued orangutans: Odisha Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory

Neither Indonesia nor any other country has so far provided documentary evidence to establish ownership of five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odisha two months ago, state Forest Minister Ganesh Ram Singh Khuntia said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Khuntia said all five orangutans were doing well , and expressed the State's desire to retain them at Nandankanan Zoological Park.
"All five baby orangutans are doing well and growing. No one should disturb them. We want them to stay in Odisha, and visitors will get an opportunity to see them at Nandankanan Zoo," he said.

The Minister said some countries might stake a claim to the animals under international wildlife trade regulations, but they would have to furnish concrete evidence to establish that the rescued animals originated from their territory.

"The Indonesian government has raised its claim as a routine matter. We will seek evidence to establish that the orangutans originated from their country. If they provide the proof, the animals may be handed over to them," Mr. Khuntia said.
He added that the State government had submitted details of the rescued animals to the Centre for necessary action.
"Odisha has a conducive environment for orangutans. So, we want them to stay here," he said.
The five baby orangutans were rescued from Bichitrapur forest in Balasore district on September 8 and subsequently shifted to Nandankanan Zoo, where they have been kept in quarantine.
Officials said the animals were housed in a temperature-controlled room and were gradually acclimatising to the local environment.

The State government has made arrangements for their comfort and to help them overcome stress. The animals have displayed a range of emotions, from playful behaviour and brief mood swings to anxiously clinging to one another, they said.

Nandankanan Zoo already has a special enclosure for orangutans, which has remained vacant since the death of a 41-year-old female orangutan in 2019. The animal had been brought from a Pune zoo in 2003, they added.
A joint investigation by the Odisha Police's Special Task Force (STF) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) is underway to ascertain how the orangutans reached Balasore.

articles.title: Poland mourns victims of Krakow mass shooting as security fears grow
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Seventeen people, including two police officers and the gunman, were wounded in the attack, authorities said

Poland began two days of national mourning on Sunday (November 8, 2026) ‌and police bolstered security after six people were killed in a mass ​shooting in Krakow that authorities said was likely inspired by far-right ideology.

Saturday’s ⁠(November 7) attack in the city’s historic main square shocked a country that has prided itself on being safer than many of its Western European neighbours, deepening public concern following a string of school stabbings ‌in October that officials linked to extremist content online.
Seventeen people, including two police officers and the gunman, were wounded in the attack, authorities said.
The ‌24-year-old suspect’s parents and sister were later found dead at their home, and ‌he ⁠remained in hospital in a critical condition, police and a local official ⁠said.

In Krakow, the old town’s main market square and the surrounding streets remained closed, with police allowing only essential workers to pass. Many nearby cafes were closed and flags at the ​city hall were at half-mast. Mourners ‌placed candles in several locations in the area.
The traditional trumpet call from St Mary’s church on the square was suspended for 12 hours to commemorate the dead, the first time this has happened since 1939, state news agency PAP reported.

In the capital, ‌Warsaw, police said on Saturday (November 7) they were strengthening security measures in busy ​areas popular with tourists. Barriers were installed on streets leading onto the Krakowskie Przedmiescie street in the historic heart of the capital.
In the suspect’s home ⁠town, Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 200 km (124 miles) north of Krakow, police said they had found the bodies of his parents and sister and that investigations were ongoing.

“Yesterday, before 22:00, we ‌discovered the bodies of three individuals — a 53-year-old man and two women, aged 52 and 21 — in an apartment located in a residential building in the centre of Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski,” police wrote on X.
Maria, a 20-year-old Warsaw cafe employee, said she “almost burst into tears” when she heard about the attack in Krakow.
“Recent events — not just this one, but things happening lately — are really affecting our sense of security,” ‌she said.
Leading daily newspaper Rzeczpospolita said in an editorial that the mass shooting brought a “brutal end ​to an era in which Poland was considered an island of safety”.

articles.title: Bangladesh Law Minister calls Hasina ‘convicted criminal’, says extradition request sent to India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian govt previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over

Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday (November 8, 2026) described ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as a "convicted criminal" and said Dhaka has requested India to extradite her, according to local media reports.

Responding to questions from journalists after inaugurating a training workshop in Dhaka, Mr. Asaduzzaman said the government was taking all necessary legal steps to bring Ms. Hasina back from India and would follow due process.
"To me, she is a criminal. A criminal convicted by our tribunal. To us, this is her identity," he said, according to a report on bdnews24 website.
Asked about bringing Ms. Hasina back to Bangladesh, the Law Minister said the government would act in accordance with the law and would not be guided by emotion.

"Although the Law Ministry is not directly involved in this matter, the Ministry of Home Affairs is concerned, as it relates to the extradition treaty with India. The matter will be dealt with in accordance with the law, leaving no room for emotions. We have requested her repatriation under the treaty and through due process," Mr. Asaduzzaman was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency.
Bdnews24 also quoted Mr. Asaduzzaman as saying: "That is a matter for the Indian government. We have made requests to them under the extradition treaty."
"If they hand her over to us, we will hand her over in the due process, as required under the law," he added.

India has previously acknowledged receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Ms. Hasina but has not announced any decision on handing her over. The Ministry of External Affairs has said the requests are being examined as part of its established processes.
Ms. Hasina fled Bangladesh for India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising that ended her 15-year rule. An interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus subsequently took charge.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Sheikh Hasina speaks to The Hindu : Bangladesh protests, India and her return plans

Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 convicted Ms. Hasina of crimes against humanity committed during the July-August 2024 uprising. The tribunal, which tried her in absentia, sentenced her to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another.
In February this year, Bangladesh held parliamentary elections and the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) led by Tarique Rahman formed the government.
