articles.title: Crew member missing as Indonesian water-bombing helicopter crashes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A helicopter battling Indonesian wildfires crashed into a river on Sunday as it scooped water, an official told AFP , with two crew members rescued and one still missing.

The crash in Borneo Island's South Kalimantan province was the second in days involving a firefighting helicopter, after a military chopper plunged into the waters off Borneo on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), killing three people.

Two Australian nationals had survived Sunday's (November 8, 2026) incident and were "safe", said Berton Panjaitan, a spokesman for the national disaster mitigation agency, while the third member of the crew, an Indonesian, remained unaccounted for.
Dramatic video footage showed the firefighting helicopter being slowly dragged downward after filling its bucket from the Barito River, eventually plunging nose-first into the water.

The Southeast Asian archipelago has for months been struggling to control blazes that have burned through large swathes of Sumatra, Borneo and Papua islands, causing choking haze that drifted to neighbouring Malaysia, East Timor and Singapore.
"This incident occurred while the air fleet was conducting a water-bombing operation," spokesman Berton said of Sunday's crash.
"In footage captured by an amateur video, the helicopter appears to lose control while manoeuvring after scooping up water from the river with a bambi bucket."
The Eurocopter EC225LP Super Puma belonged to a company the disaster mitigation agency had contracted for water-bombing operations, he added.
On Wednesday, a helicopter carrying eight people crashed during a mission to fight fires in Tanjung Puting National Park, home to animals including critically endangered Bornean orangutans.
The incident occurred while the aircraft was scooping seawater for water bombing, according to an army statement, which added that the accident's cause was under investigation.

Aside from ground-based firefighters, Indonesia has relied heavily on air operations to fight the fires that have destroyed more than 1.9 million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires are driven in part by a strong El Nino weather phenomenon, which in Indonesia typically causes drought.

articles.title: Taiwan detains Communist Party leader over alleged Chinese sponsorship in election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Authorities in Taiwan detained the leader of the island's Taiwan People's Communist Party, accusing him of running as a candidate for borough chief under the direction and sponsorship of China's Communist Party, local media reported on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

Taiwan is set to hold elections for mayors and local area chiefs on November 28. While the races focus more on livelihood issues, the results could be a good indicator of the popularity of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party under the leadership of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te ahead of the presidential election in 2028.

According to Taiwan's Central News Agency, prosecutors said in a statement on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that an initial investigation showed Taiwan People's Communist Party chair Lin Te-wang also had directed another party member to run as a candidate for chief in another borough.
Prosecutors also alleged that Mr. Lin sought to buy votes by repeatedly recruiting voters to travel to mainland China, where they received hospitality, the report said.

While Mr. Lin's party is not influential on the democratic island, it was not his first legal trouble over his alleged links with China. He and another party leader had faced charges of Chinese infiltration and attempting to influence elections but were found not guilty in 2025, the Taipei Times reported.
Taiwan's Central News Agency said the prosecutors had received intelligence about foreign interference in the election and summoned 14 people and nine witnesses.

After questioning, the government lawyers strongly suspected that Lin and the other party member had committed a crime and were concerned the pair could flee or destroy evidence, so they filed applications to the local courts to detain them and bar them from being visited by others, it said.

The courts ruled in the prosecutors' favour for Lin but released the other member on a 50,000-Taiwan-dollar ($1,525) bail, the news agency said. The other people summoned were released during the investigation, it added.
China's Taiwan Affairs Office has not immediately commented.
Beijing views Taiwan as a breakaway province to be retaken by force if necessary, and claims of China's meddling are common in Taiwanese elections.

China and Taiwan have been governed separately since 1949 when the Chinese Communist Party rose to power in Beijing following a civil war. Defeated Nationalist Party forces fled to Taiwan, which later transitioned from martial law to multiparty democracy.

articles.title: Riyadh financial district targeted in missile attack, Aramco tower damaged: witnesses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, said another witness, with glass shattered and damage to part of the tower's facade visible

Multiple witnesses told A FP o n Sunday (November 8, 2026) that Riyadh's financial district was targeted and the area's Aramco tower was damaged, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.
"Aramco tower in KAFD has been targeted, that's the sure thing," said one witness, referring to the King Abdullah Financial District. Two other witnesses confirmed seeing damage to the building.

A 2022 truce that had paused fighting in Yemen's long-running conflict fell apart in July and Saudi Arabia has since traded blows with the Houthis, who have struck Saudi airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
The Iran-backed Houthis seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014, with the Saudi-led coalition entering the conflict a year later in support of the government.

The King Abdullah Financial District is one of the most visible manifestations of the kingdom's ongoing economic and social reforms drive, with towering glass skyscrapers, high-end retail outlets and green spaces dotting the area.
Targeting the district would mark a major escalation in the kingdom's fight with the Houthis.
The area is also home to residential housing and a large metro station with heavy commuter traffic during the morning rush hour.
Multiple floors of the Aramco tower appeared to have sustained damage, said another witness, with glass shattered and damage to part of the tower's facade visible.

The attack comes hours after the Kingdom's education ministry announced, late on Saturday (November 7, 2026), the return of in-person schooling after weeks of remote-learning in Riyadh following an earlier wave of strikes.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki, in a Sunday (November 8, 2026) morning social media post, said that "air defences intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards Riyadh", as loud explosions were heard in the Saudi capital.
The Kingdom has been pressing allies for help as it comes under daily fire from the Houthis that recently seized swathes of the Red Sea coastline from the Riyadh-backed government.
Thousands of Syrian troops are set to deploy to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with some already on the ground, multiple Yemeni officials told AFP .

articles.title: Fresh sexual harassment complaint against ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Action has been initiated based on the statement of the minor, who was previously a witness in an already registered case

In a fresh development in the ongoing probe against granite baron R Veeramani , who is facing charges of sexually harassing minors, another girl has come forward with a complaint of harassment, police said on Sunday.
Action has been initiated based on the statement of the minor, who was previously a witness in an already registered case, they said.

The case traces back to October 2025 when a child rights activist handed over a pen drive to the Anti-Vice Squad containing a video of a minor being sexually assaulted. A note accompanying the drive alleged that the man in the footage was Veeramani and that the incident occurred at the residence of Mahendra Simhan and Shanthi.

Although the police initially attempted to file a closure report citing an inability to identify the victim, a Special POCSO court judge rejected the move in February 2026 and ordered further investigation.
Following the court's intervention, police recovered the original video during searches and subsequently arrested Mr. Veeramani, Ms. Shanthi, and Mahendra Simhan in August 2026.
A Special Investigation Team was later constituted to probe the allegations.
The police have now registered a total of eight cases concerning the sexual harassment of minors. Mr. Veeramani has been arrested in all eight cases.

The other accused include Ms. Shanthi, arrested in three cases, Lazar in five cases, Mahendra Simhan in two cases, and Ganesan in two cases. Srinivasan, Sakthivel, Babu, and Parthiban have been arrested in one case each.
All the accused are currently lodged at the Puzhal Central Prison in Chennai.

During the ongoing investigation, accused driver Mr. Lazar was taken into one-day police custody for interrogation. Based on this inquiry, authorities identified a white car used in the crime and initiated subsequent action.
Meanwhile, a POCSO court Judge directed the Tamil Nadu government to grant a relief fund of ₹2 lakh to one of the victims.
Out of the eight registered cases, the police are scheduled to file the final reports for two cases in the coming week.

articles.title: Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota cremated in his native place Mansa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13

The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
A large number of people had turned up when last rites were held after his body was brought here from Chandigarh, following a post-mortem at PGIMER on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
The cremation was held at Jhota’s fields on Chakerian Road.

Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.
A number of people also turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.
Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.
“I thank the joint action committee which stood by us all through,” he told reporters on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota’s murder.

Jhota’s body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on Wednesday (November 4).
The anti-drug activist’s family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist.
On October 28, two JAC members, Lakhvir Singh and Mohanjit Singh Sheron, were arrested during the protest.

On the evening of November 5, the JAC members were released from Nabha district jail after a meeting between the protesters and government representatives, including Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, on November 4.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Jhota was shot dead in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town on October 13

The mortal remains of slain anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, whose murder 26 days ago triggered protests and a political row, were consigned to flames at his native place here on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

A large number of people had turned up when last rites were held after his body was brought here from Chandigarh, following a post-mortem at PGIMER on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The cremation was held at Jhota’s fields on Chakerian Road.

Jhota was shot dead on October 13 in broad daylight at a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa town while he was hosting a Facebook Live session. The store owner, who had fired at Jhota after the activist confronted him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man, was subsequently arrested.

A number of people also turned up at his home to pay their last respects before the cremation was held.

Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, called upon the youth of Punjab to pledge against drug abuse, saying his son gave up his life fighting against the scourge.

“I thank the joint action committee which stood by us all through,” he told reporters on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

The joint action committee (JAC), also known as the Parminder Singh Jhota Insaaf Action Committee, is a coalition of various social organisations and activists formed in Punjab after Jhota’s murder.

Jhota’s body was brought to PGIMER Chandigarh from the mortuary of Civil Hospital in Mansa in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), after his family ended their 22-day agitation and agreed to a post-mortem following a meeting with Punjab government representatives on Wednesday (November 4).

The anti-drug activist’s family, along with the JAC, had been sitting on a protest in Mansa seeking justice for the slain activist.

On October 28, two JAC members, Lakhvir Singh and Mohanjit Singh Sheron, were arrested during the protest.

On the evening of November 5, the JAC members were released from Nabha district jail after a meeting between the protesters and government representatives, including Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khudian, on November 4.

articles.title: H.D. Kumaraswamy alleges Hassan DC retained her post by paying bribe to district in-charge Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy has alleged that the Hassan Deputy Commissioner retained her post by paying ₹75 lakh to Excise Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also the in-charge Minister of Hassan district.

Speaking to presspersons in Hassan after visiting the historic Hasanamba temple in Hassan on Sunday (November 8, 2026), Mr. Kumaraswamy read out excerpts from a written script of what he described as a WhatsApp conversation between an unidentified person and Shashikiran, the personal assistant to the Hassan Deputy Commissioner. He said he received the contents of the conversation from an official who met him the previous night.

According to Mr. Kumaraswamy, the conversation was about seeking permission for three stone crushers. The personal assistant allegedly demanded ₹60 lakh to get the clearance. As the person on the other end bargained, Mr. Shashikiran is said to have listed the people with whom the amount had to be shared.

Mr. Kumaraswamy said the conversation also mentioned that Mr. Shivalinge Gowda wanted to transfer the incumbent Deputy Commissioner from Hassan. However, she allegedly managed to convince the Minister by paying ₹75 lakh through Arsikere Tahsildar Santosh.
The script of the purported conversation was also distributed to journalists. Mr. Kumaraswamy said it also referred to the Hassan MP and several officials of the district.
He demanded an investigation into the allegations and urged the police to seize the mobile phone from the person concerned for further examination.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who also visited the temple the same day, said the Deputy Commissioner had been doing a good job. “However, allegations are being made against her because she did not yield to their demands,” he said.

Hassan Deputy Commissioner K.S. Latha Kumari has denied the allegations made against her, saying she has never done anything illegal. “I have not done anything wrong, I am not doing anything wrong, and I will never do anything wrong,” she said.

Ms. Kumari said that if any wrong message had been sent by her personal assistant or anyone in his section, proper action would be taken. She condemned the circulation of “false and baseless information”. “Let there be an inquiry. Those who have erred should face action,” she said.
She said a complaint would be filed with the cyber police, as spreading false information was a crime. “We will bring out the truth,” she added.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Guards did not specify the names or nationality of the tankers

Three oil tankers caught fire on Sunday (November 8, 2026) in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran regularly targets ships that transit without its authorisation, the Revolutionary Guards said in a statement.
Since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.
The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

“Since the early hours of this morning, three non-compliant tankers have exploded and caught fire while they were sailing in the illegal channel in the Strait of Hormuz,” the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement.

Also on Sunday, British maritime agency UKMTO reported that a tanker had caught fire in the strait — off the coast of Khasab, Oman — a day earlier.

“Military authorities reported the tanker is on fire which has resulted in the evacuation of the crew,” the agency said in a statement, also reporting another tanker struck by an “unknown projectile” on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Emirati state media said on Sunday that 22 people had been rescued from a burning vessel in the Gulf of Oman and were in stable condition. AFP was unable to confirm if the various reports referenced the same incidents.
Tehran has made multiple announcements in recent weeks saying that ships have caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer and has recently said that all mines have been cleared from the waterway.
Iranian state news agency IRNA separately reported late on Saturday (November 7, 2026) that sounds of explosions were heard in parts of the country.
“Sounds resembling explosions were heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask and Bandar Abbas. The cause of the sounds remains unknown,” the news agency wrote on Telegram.

articles.title: U.S. launches task force to disrupt land transit routes into Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies
The U.S. military has announced it will create a 20-member task force to find ways to disrupt land routes into Iran that it says are used for shipments of weapons and illicit materials.

The restrictions would expand on a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports during the two countries' eight-month war, in which Tehran has also restricted passage through the critical Strait of Hormuz trade route, choking global energy supplies.

The task force's work "will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a statement posted on X on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

The team of both civilian and military personnel based in Florida would coordinate with U.S. government agencies on "preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea," the statement added.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Washington's latest bid "will fail" and will not bring about economic collapse in the Islamic republic.

"The United States will never be able to impose the economic blockade it is pursuing and proposing under various names and through different plans," Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.
"The Americans will not achieve their objective of exerting extreme economic pressure to bring about the collapse and disintegration of Iran's economy."
Mr. Mohebi added that the United States would be "powerless to block" communication channels between Iran and neighbouring countries.
CENTCOM said that the naval blockade on Iranian ports had "prevented Iran from exporting more than $25 billion in crude oil."
In August, Washington announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign on Iran aimed at strangling its already battered economy.
Those measures were in response to Tehran's blockade of the Hormuz strait, where Iranian forces have regularly targeted vessels that attempted to cross without authorisation.

articles.title: Jean Drèze urges T.N. govt. to take strict action amid report of ‘fake book’ at Kalaignar Centenary Library
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” the economist said in a clarification via e-mail to The Hindu
Economist Jean Drèze on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said an English-language book attributed to him as the author and allegedly found in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu is “fake”.

The confirmation comes following a media report alleging that a title listed in Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library may not have been authored by Mr. Drèze. The book which lists him as the author was identified as the title ‘ Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World’’.

“I am foxed and baffled to read on social media that a book called Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World, attributed to me, has surfaced in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu. If this book exists under my name, it must be fake, because I have never authored such a book,” he wrote in a clarification issued to The Hindu via e-mail.

Mr. Drèze urged the Tamil Nadu government to take “strict and swift action against the publishers of this fake book and other culprits”. “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” he added.

The economist also raised questions on procurement checks in place at public libraries and said: “The issue is not just that a fake book was printed but also how it was procured by a public library. Surely it would have taken little effort to ascertain the authenticity of this book.”

According to the media report, the book in question was allegedly procured from Phoenix Publishers and carries a valid International Standard Book Number. It also further alleged that the address of Phoenix Publishers is the same as that of Akal Vilakku Publishers.

The procurement date cited in the report is June 25, 2023 before the inauguration of the library. Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library was inaugurated on July 15, 2023, by the then Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.

articles.title: Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water to be used for mist spraying in Kolkata; environmentalist slams move
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water will be mixed into mist spraying on special occasions, while environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh says the city’s air needs cleaning at the source

West Bengal Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul has said that, on special occasions, rose water will be mixed with the water normally used for mist spraying to control air pollution in the city.
The move drew criticism from an environmentalist, who argued that the city’s air needed to be cleaned at the source rather than through such cosmetic interventions.

In a Facebook post in Bengali, Ms. Paul said the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has regularly been spraying water mist at various locations across the city, particularly in areas where the Air Quality Index (AQI) is relatively high. This was being done under the direction of the State government to control air pollution in Kolkata and make the city’s environment cleaner.

articles.title: West Bengal to institute 'Seema Mitra' award for BSF, SSB, police personnel from 2027: Suvendu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.
"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.
The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.
The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.
Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.
He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.
Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.
He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.
He claimed that the people gave their "appropriate retort" through the democratic process.
The Trinamool Congress lost to the BJP in the 2026 assembly elections in the State.

articles.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident

The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said.
Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition.
All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL.
One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day.
A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said.
A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement.
An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation.
Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said.

The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added.
The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person.
Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma were closely monitoring the situation, the PSU said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Mr. Sonowal, who is the Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh, called OIL CMD Ranjit Rath to take stock of the situation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Sonowal, who is the Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh, called OIL CMD Ranjit Rath to take stock of the situation.

articles.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Green Tribunal takes suo motu cognisance of The Hindu report

The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss.

Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector.

The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.”
The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction.

It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani.

Pollution, habitat destruction, loss of riparian vegetation, invasive fish and aquatic plants, use of soaps and shampoos by people bathing in the river, rituals performed on its banks, dumping of puja materials and clothes, and discharge of untreated sewage have contributed to the decline in fish populations.

articles.title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

“These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Celebrating Diwali with CRPF personnel in Bastar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country must “identify and defeat” ideological supporters of Naxalism who have “infiltrated” parties and organisations

Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

Diwali is sweeter with those who protect us! #Bastar #NaxalFreeIndia https://t.co/7Ywie7uTt4

The Prime Minister said the government had taken tough decisions to strengthen national security, including measures not widely known.

“These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

articles.title: Turkey, Azerbaijan leaders vow unity after tensions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Turkic-speaking allies describe their relationship as "one nation, two states" and, despite the friction, remain closely bound by military and energy ties

Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that their countries' alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
Tensions flared in September, when Baku revised school uniform regulations to prohibit clothing deemed incompatible with secular education, effectively barring Islamic headscarves in classrooms.
Mr. Erdogan's government has dismantled restrictions on hijabs in Turkey.

Azerbaijan's move sparked protests at home and drew criticism from Mr. Erdogan's Islamist-rooted Justice and Development Party (AKP). Presidential adviser Oktay Saral demanded that Azerbaijan reverse the restrictions.
Baku also declared 31 Turkish nationals, including an Opposition lawmaker and party leaders, persona non grata over critical social media posts.

Mr. Erdogan subsequently dismissed Mr. Saral, but Mr. Aliyev stayed away from an October 30 summit of Turkic leaders in Ankara — despite a personal invitation from Mr. Erdogan. Instead, he sent Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov.

On Sunday (November 8, 2026), as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Mr. Erdogan arrived in the country's Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
A guard of honour lined up at the airport, where Mr. Aliyev and First Lady Mehriban Aliyeva, welcomed Mr. Erdogan and his wife Ms. Emine.
"With the permission of Almighty God, our unity will endure forever," Mr. Erdogan told a joint press conference with Mr. Aliyev.
"This unity of hearts, which we describe with the motto 'One Nation, Two States,' is an everlasting torch that draws strength from our shared past and illuminates our future."
Mr. Aliyev said the alliance — "an important factor across a vast geographical area" — remained unshaken.
"Together, Azerbaijan and Turkey are even stronger," he said, adding that Mr. Erdogan's visit "shows the whole world our unity".

articles.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills four, injures 88 others: Health Ministry
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster
Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday (November 8, 2026), derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities.
Egypt's railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
The Health Ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area.
State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury.

President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident "with great concern", and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to "hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza's Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt's worst-ever rail disaster.
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt's 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network.

articles.title: 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Fighting in the Ruweng administrative area has left 23 dead and thousands displaced, officials said, as South Sudan heads towards elections on December 22

Four weeks of clashes between South Sudan government and opposition forces in the north of the impoverished country have left 23 people dead while thousands have fled the conflict zone, authorities and police said Sunday.

Hundreds of people have died in clashes across South Sudan in recent weeks between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of detained former vice president Riek Machar and other ethnic unrest, as the world's youngest country heads towards national elections scheduled for December 22.
Ruweng administrative area's information minister Tony Chol Ayat told AFP that fighters from Riek Machar's SPLA-IO force had entered Ruweng from neighbouring Unity state.
He said fighting between October 4 and Thursday this week had left 23 dead and 17 wounded. The toll was confirmed by two police sources.
Chol Ayat said that more than 100,000 people had fled the fighting while one of the police sources confirmed "thousands" had left the area.
A resident in Ruweng told AFP that SPLA-IO fighters had started fighting and that "the government built up forces on the front lines and the rebel armies were repelled".
Another Ruweng resident said there were fears of heightened conflict. Both spoke on condition of anonymity.
A South Sudan army spokesman would not comment on events, while Riek Machar's forces did not respond to an AFP query.

Independent since 2011, South Sudan is one of the world's poorest countries with widespread corruption. Saalva Kiir and Riek Machar's forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that left more than 400,000 dead.

The country's first presidential and legislative election has already been postponed several times and a UN human rights commission, which has accused the country's elite of siphoning off billions of dollars of oil revenues, has said an election in current tensions could unleash widespread new conflict.

articles.title: Europe will be represented at U.S.-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi: France
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table
Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTL radio .
His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.
The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.
Mr. Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with," but "this time they will participate".
He said, "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."
On Thursday (November 5, 2026), U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.
A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

Jared Kushner, the U.S. President's envoy and son-in-law, participated in the Brussels meeting by videolink. He said the United States was working on "a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace".
The American approach is being treated warily by European allies, which have long rejected Moscow's desire to rewrite the European security architecture.

articles.title: Poland calls Krakow shooting rampage 'terrorist' attack
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, says an Interior Ministry spokeswoman

Poland on Sunday (November 88, 2026) launched a terrorism probe as mourners brought candles and flowers to Krakow's Main Market Square in tribute to six people killed by a gunman who authorities said was "fascinated by far-right ideologies".
The 24-year-old Polish man opened fire at random on Saturday (November 7) in the historic centre of the country's second city, in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk called an act of "terrorism".
A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, an Interior Ministry spokeswoman said.
Three more bodies were found at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 150 kilometres (95 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.
The gunman was wounded in a shootout with police and is in critical condition in hospital. The National Prosecutor's Office said it had launched a terrorism investigation.
"I'm absolutely devastated," Weronika Filar, 27, a Krakow resident, told AFP on Sunday (November 8).
"It's one of the safest places on Earth genuinely... I did not expect anything like this to happen to us," she said. "Our city will never be the same."

articles.title: Israel Defence Minister says 'mission not complete' on Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: "Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," says Mr. Katz
Israel is not finished with Iran, its Defence Minister said Sunday (November 8, 2026), as he also warned Tehran's Lebanese ally Hezbollah to hold fire in any resumption of war.
Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed charges that Iran — attacked twice since last year in major Israeli-U.S. bombing campaigns — is pursuing nuclear weapons, a claim that Tehran denies.

"Concerning Iran, the mission is still not complete. Iran is trying to renew its efforts to obtain nuclear weapons — alongside other grave efforts that place the State of Israel in real danger," Mr. Katz said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political life, has repeatedly threatened new strikes against Iran in recent weeks.

But it remains unclear if he has the support of U.S. President Donald Trump, his close ally, who suffered a major rebuke from voters in elections on Tuesday (November 10), in part over anger against the war.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Friday that Mr. Netanyahu and the Mossad intelligence service attempted an operation against Iran on the eve of Israel's own October 27 election but that the United States found out and stopped it.
Mr. Netanyahu has ordered a multi-nation war since the unprecedented attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, by Hamas, the Palestinian militant group in Gaza backed by Iran's clerical state.

Israel has devastated Gaza and has invaded Lebanon, after Hezbollah fired on Israel in solidarity with Iran. Israel has also moved past a former ceasefire line to occupy part of historic adversary Syria after the fall in 2024 of longtime leader Bashar al-Assad.

"We will not withdraw from the security zones in Gaza, Lebanon and Syria, and if the terrorist organisation Hezbollah chooses to join Iran in an attack on Israel, it will suffer extremely severe blows," Mr. Katz said.
Mr. Netanyahu suffered losses in the October 27 election, with his rival Gadi Eisenkot tasked with forming a new government.

Eisenkot has warned Israel's military that Mr. Netanyahu has no mandate and that it should not go to war for his "political needs", although the former army chief has largely supported Mr. Netanyahu's war decisions.

"We may argue, and we may disagree, but when the security of the state is at stake, we must know how to rise above our disputes," said Mr. Katz, who was speaking at a ceremony for Israeli troops who died in a 1956 attack on Egypt.

articles.title: AIDSO protests in Kalaburagi and Ballari against proposed closure of 45,000 government schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) staged protests in Kalaburagi and Ballari on Friday, opposing the Karnataka government’s proposed KPS Magnet school policy, which the organisation alleged would lead to the closure of around 45,000 government schools across the State.

The protests were held at Thimmapur Circle in Kalaburagi and OPD Circle in Ballari. The demonstrators condemned the Congress government for allegedly moving ahead with the policy despite strong public opposition and demanded that it withdraw the proposal and protect the public education system.

Addressing the protesters in Kalaburagi, AIDSO district president Tuljaram N.K. alleged that the government, which had promised to protect government schools before coming to power, was now preparing to close thousands of them in the name of the KPS Magnet scheme and implement the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. He claimed that the conditions mentioned in the loan agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) clearly indicated the proposed changes.
AIDSO activists staging a protest at OPD Circle in Ballari on Friday, opposing the proposed closure of 45,000 government schools under the KPS Magnet scheme. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

AIDSO State treasurer Subhash Bettadakoppa, speaking at the Ballari protest, also criticised the government for allegedly accepting conditions that would undermine the public education system. He questioned how the Congress could claim to be protecting democracy while pursuing a policy that, according to the organisation, would deprive children from poor families of access to government schools.

The speakers alleged that the ADB-linked conditions envisaged the merger of all government schools around school clusters into a single institution by 2030; financial support from corporate companies for the management of KPS Magnet schools; and a curriculum designed to prepare students as a workforce suited to the needs of those companies. They also claimed that future teacher recruitment would be restricted to KPS schools and that the government would stop providing grants to these schools after 2030.

The protesters expressed concern that the policy would leave only 4,038 schools functioning in Karnataka while resulting in the closure of around 45,000 government schools. They alleged that the State’s education policy was increasingly being shaped by foreign financial institutions and corporate interests rather than by educationists and intellectuals from Karnataka.

Abdul Waheed, president of the district committee for the protection of public education, also addressed the Kalaburagi protest. In Ballari, S.G. Nagarathna, vice-president of the committee, said the proposed policy posed a serious threat to public education and called for a united struggle to protect government schools.

Referring to the 200th birth anniversary of social reformer Jyotiba Phule, the speakers said protecting public education was a historic responsibility and warned that the organisation would intensify its agitation against the policy.

The Kalaburagi protest was presided over by AIDSO district secretary Venkatesh Devadurga. District vice-presidents Radha Preeti Doddamani and Govind Yalawar, Nagaraj Ravoor, and other members and activists participated.

In Ballari, the protest was presided over by district secretary Kambali Manjunath. AIDSO district president K. Eranna, vice-president M. Shanthi, district treasurer Anupama, office secretary Niharika, members Kantesh and Thippeswamy, and hundreds of students took part.

articles.title: Fire breaks out at high-rise building in Mumbai’s Ghatkopar East; three hospitalised
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ganesh Shinde said that the fire started while the residents were using a drill to install fairy lights in their house for Deepavali, which triggered the short circuit
Three people, including two children, were hospitalised after a fire broke out on one floor of a 25-storey residential building in Ghatkopar East on Friday evening (November 6, 2026).

The fire has been brought under control, with the police suspecting a short circuit as the preliminary cause of the blaze. No fatalities have been reported and the condition of all three in the hospital was reported to be stable.
According to a statement issued by the Mayor’s Office, the Mumbai Fire Brigade, the entire building was evacuated as a precautionary measure.

Three people were reported injured in the incident. According to an update received from the on-duty Assistant Medical Officer (AMO) at 9.25 p.m., Sainath Awale (45) sustained 27% burn injuries and was reported to be in stable condition. Meanwhile, Dr. Rozbin of Zynova Hospital confirmed at 10.40 p.m. that two other injured persons, identified as Nirav Lodaya (34) and Rajesh Lodaya (47), had been admitted to the hospital. Both were reported to be in stable condition.

The incident occurred on the 23rd floor of the Royal Altezza building on Vallabh Baug Lane in Pant Nagar. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) received information about the blaze at 8.08 p.m.
The fire brigade initially declared a Level-I fire call at 8.30 p.m, which was subsequently escalated to Level-II at 8.52 p.m.

Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde visited the site on Friday night (November 6, 2026) and reviewed the ongoing rescue and relief operations. Local MLA Parag Shah and corporators Suresh Awale and Dharmesh Giri were also present at the spot.

DCP (East Zone 2) Ganesh Shinde said that the fire started while the residents were using a drill to install fairy lights in their house for Deepavali, which triggered the short circuit. Now, the building will be shut till the Fire Department and the Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited ask to reopen. The residents were requested to get food to eat and stay with neighbours or family in the city for the night.
After safety and security checks by the Mumbai Fire Brigade and the Mumbai police, wings C and D of the building were cleared for residents to return to.
According to the Chief Fire Officer, the blaze has been brought under control. One injured person was shifted to Rajawadi Hospital, where their condition was reported to be stable.
Two children who suffered from suffocation were taken to Zynova Hospital.
Personnel from the Mumbai Fire Brigade, police, the electricity distribution company, the Public Works Department (PWD) and the BMC’s ward staff were mobilised following the incident.

The fire has been brought under control, with the police suspecting a short circuit as the preliminary cause of the blaze. No fatalities have been reported and the condition of all three in the hospital was reported to be stable.

According to a statement issued by the Mayor’s Office, the Mumbai Fire Brigade, the entire building was evacuated as a precautionary measure.

Three people were reported injured in the incident. According to an update received from the on-duty Assistant Medical Officer (AMO) at 9.25 p.m., Sainath Awale (45) sustained 27% burn injuries and was reported to be in stable condition. Both were reported to be in stable condition.

The incident occurred on the 23rd floor of the Royal Altezza building on Vallabh Baug Lane in Pant Nagar. According to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) received information about the blaze at 8.08 p.m.

articles.title: Students urged to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths, and continuously upgrade skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, say speakers at a career seminar organised by The Hindu FIC

Students must take ownership of their careers, identify their strengths and aspirations, and continuously upgrade their skills to succeed in an evolving professional landscape, said Prof. Satya Duvvuri of the Paari School of Business, SRM University-AP.

Addressing students at a seminar on ‘Career Opportunities in Management & Technology’, organised by The Hindu FIC and Paari School of Business, SRM AP, he urged them to explore opportunities beyond conventional career paths and make informed choices driven by their interests and determination.

Through real-life examples, anecdotes and interactive discussions, Prof. Satya highlighted how several successful professionals from engineering and science backgrounds had utilised their technical knowledge to emerge as prominent leaders in diverse fields.
He emphasised that passion, perseverance and a willingness to learn could open doors to limitless career opportunities.
Logo for The Hindu FIC & SRM AP seminar on careers in management and technology

He underlined the growing importance of analytical thinking, comprehension and proficiency in emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), in preparing students for future careers. Encouraging them to dream big, work hard and pursue their passions, he said opportunities were often closer than they imagined and that their future depended largely on their own choices and efforts.

Executive Director of Kallam Haranadhareddy Institute of Technology (KHIT) Navya Kallam said that the world offered opportunities across diverse sectors and that engineering graduates could explore areas beyond their core disciplines.
She pointed out that skills such as accounting, which is considered the backbone of any business, could help students become successful entrepreneurs.
KHIT Director Uma Shankar Reddy observed that there was no age limit for acquiring new skills.

Citing the example of the institution’s founder K. Haranadhareddy, who learnt music at the age of 75 and performed at temples, he encouraged students to remain open to learning throughout their lives. He also stressed that higher educational qualifications could strengthen career prospects, noting that additional qualifications often offered an advantage in career advancement and promotions.

Principal of KHIT, Guntur district, B.S.B. Reddy said that rapid technological advancements and the convergence of different technologies were transforming the employment landscape. While certain job roles were becoming obsolete, new opportunities were emerging simultaneously. He expressed confidence that the seminar would help students gain clarity, build confidence and address uncertainties about their career choices.
Executive Director, KHIT, KHM Bharadwaj, Assistant Director, SRM-AP V.V.S. Pradeep and V. Amar from The Hindu were among those participated in the programme.

articles.title: 12 of family injured in fire caused by CNG leak in M.P.'s Orchha; two of them critical
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Scrap dealer Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire

Twelve members of a family, including three children, suffered burn injuries in a fire that broke out following a CNG leak at a scrap shop in Madhya Pradesh's Orchha town on Friday (November 6, 2026), police said.

The injured were taken to a hospital in Jhansi in neighbouring Uttar Pradesh for treatment, and the condition of two of them — scrap dealer Khalil (60) and his son Sameer (30) — is stated to be critical, Orchha police station house officer Jitendra Singh Gurjar told PTI .
Mr. Khalil had purchased a CNG cylinder from someone and was trying to dismantle it to extract brass and other metals when the gas leaked out of it and sparked a fire, he said.
The blaze engulfed the premises, causing 12 members of Mr. Khalil's family to suffer burn injuries, he said.

Niwari Superintendent of Police Rai Singh Narwaria and District Collector Jamuna Bhide reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, and arranged for the injured to be shifted to the Jhansi medical hospital, the inspector said.
No case has been registered in connection with the incident so far, Mr. Gurjar said, adding that the police would take action based on the investigation.

articles.title: Delhi’s Mustafabad election official lodges police complaint seeking FIR over false Form 7s filing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Delhi’s north east District Election Officer (DEO) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that they have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated

The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) of Mustafabad constituency has lodged a police complaint on Friday (November 7, 2026) seeking FIR under Section 31 of RP Act against the BLA following The Hindu’s report that false Form 7s have been filed seeking deletions of voters who are living at their addresses.

The north east District Election Officer (DEO ) Ajay Kumar told The Hindu that election officials have verified the news report independently and found 36 of the 37 Form 7s to be false/fabricated. “In connection with reports appearing in print and social media regarding false and fabricated Form-7, a police complaint has been lodged today by the ERO for registration of an FIR under Section 31 of the RP 1950 against the BLA,” a press release from his office also stated.

The Hindu reported on October 30 that in polling part area 129 of Mustafabad constituency, 28 Form 7s seeking deletions of electors found to be living in the area were filed by a BLA registered under Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Chandra Shekhar Nainwal, as per Election Commission of India (ECI) records till October 28. While Mr. Nainwal denied filing these applications and any association with BJP, speaking to The Hindu , nine fresh applications were filed naming him as objector on October 29-30. The reasons cited in these applications were “absent/permanently shifted” and “dead”.

It further said that all 37 forms were scrutinised by the BLO/AERO who found that three electors who were claimed to be dead were found alive at their addresses. All others were also found living at their addresses, as reported by The Hindu .

“Only one case is found to be true whereas 36 cases are found to be false/fabricated. Since the BLA/Objector has knowingly made false statement or declaration in the Form-7, action under Section 31 of the RP act has been invoked for making false statement /declaration in writing in connection with preparation /revision of electoral roll,” the release mentioned.

It stated that verification and inquiry in respect of other Form-7 applications is in progress. As per The Hindu analysis, over 77% of the total 1,021 Form 7s received till November 3 names 20 BJP BLAs as objector. All are against Muslim electors, and several have been found residing at their addresses in different areas.
“Necessary action, as per the guidelines of the Election Commission of India and the extant Act, shall be taken,” the DEO stated in the press release.
Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest.

“Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed.

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants.

It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC).

Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. Noting that so far only around 40 gram sabhas had become functional to commence the process of inviting claims, the government gave a last opportunity of 30 days to the State government to complete the formation of the remaining gram sabhas. The process of adjudication of the claims would be concluded within a period of five months from the date of constitution of the gram sabhas.

The court further constituted a ‘special committee’ chaired by former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai to supervise the expeditious disposal of claims and scrutinise the orders passed by the competent authorities under the 2006 Act.

The Supreme Court directed the CEC to furnish an opinion regarding the government’s view that silk cotton was a ‘minor forest produce’. This is significant for the biosphere. Presently, 3,637.83.2 hectares of the 5,072.64.3 hectares of forest land is under silk cotton cultivation.

Giving a prima facie view against the State’s claim of historical cultivation of silk cotton, the court said “what emerges from the government affidavits is the promotion and sponsored cultivation of silk cotton as a commercial crop”.

“The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce. If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change… The fact that large swathes of forest are being destroyed under the garb of cultivation of silk cotton,” the court observed.

Separately, the court directed the CEC to examine the National Highway Authority of India’s proposal relating to NH-744, including the proposed Puliara–Edamon tunnel section, which requires permission for diversion of a limited extent of reserved forest land in the biosphere.

“The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crops is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce. If commercial crops are permitted to be cultivated in the forest areas, the very nature of the forest is bound to change… The fact that large swathes of forest are being destroyed under the garb of cultivation of silk cotton,” the court observed.

Separately, the court directed the CEC to examine the National Highway Authority of India’s proposal relating to NH-744, including the proposed Puliara–Edamon tunnel section, which requires permission for diversion of a limited extent of reserved forest land in the biosphere.
