articles.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State is drawing up a ₹20,000-crore project pipeline and a series of policy measures to prepare its cities for rising temperatures and erratic rainfall. The plan, which also includes waste reclamation, sewage treatment and digital monitoring of water supply, seeks to build climate resilience across urban local bodies

From bamboo bus shelters that offer shade and cooling to commuters, to the reclamation of waste dumps and the plugging of water supply leaks, Telangana is drawing up a broad plan to make its cities more resilient to climate change. The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), said Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

The roadmap seeks to integrate climate concerns into urban planning, infrastructure development and municipal services across urban local bodies (ULBs), Municipal Administration and Urban Development secretary T.K. Sreedevi said. The policy framework is being strengthened through a mandatory Urban Road Code, a Cool Roof Policy, a Heatwave Action Plan and a Treated Water Reuse Policy. Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.

Heatwaves and erratic rainfall are becoming increasingly evident across Telangana, though their impact varies by region. The government says this calls for location-specific interventions based on climate data. The challenge is significant: the State’s cities account for net emissions of about 66.56 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, with buildings, transport, wastewater, waste management and urban expansion among the major contributors.

Some interventions are already under way. Bamboo misting bus shelters in Khammam use a low-carbon building material while providing relief to commuters. Bio-mining of legacy waste dumps is aimed at reducing methane emissions and reclaiming land. The government is also working to reduce non-revenue water through leak detection, pipeline renewal and digital monitoring, besides expanding underground sewerage networks and reusing treated wastewater.
The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

To coordinate these efforts, a State Climate Centre for Cities has been established at the office of the Commissioner and Director of Municipal Administration. It will coordinate city-level climate action plans, maintain a climate data repository and provide technical support to municipalities.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and Kothagudem.

The Telangana Urban Climate Atlas, a climate intelligence platform, has been set up to help municipalities identify vulnerable zones, prioritise investments and track climate indicators. Capacity-building programmes have been conducted for representatives of 113 ULBs to strengthen preparedness and project planning.

A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028. It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies. Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs. They can lower indoor temperatures by 2.1°C to 4.3°C and reduce air-conditioning costs by up to 20%. Full implementation is expected to save nearly 600 million units of electricity annually and generate a one-time carbon offset of about 30 million tonnes of carbon dioxide.

The policy covers government and commercial buildings and residential properties on plots of 600 square yards and above. Compliance has been integrated into the ‘Build Now’ building approval system and linked to occupancy certification. The government has also set a three-year target for retrofitting all non-residential buildings.

Urban heat mitigation proposals for Ramagundam and Adilabad are being prepared under UCF financing. Both cities are among the 29 ULBs covered by the World Bank-supported Telangana Urban Transformation and Jobs Programme, which includes urban greening, shaded public spaces and cool-roof measures.

articles.title: Karnataka CM ridicules BJP leaders for trying to take credit for PM’s visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take credit for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the metro Pink Line, even though he was arriving on the official invitation of the State government.

Without taking the name of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, the Chief Minister alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take publicity by claiming that they were responsible for the Prime Minsiter’s proposed visit.
Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it.
“We are developing metro network by borrowing money. I will present some of these issues before the Prime Minister on November 13,” he said.

articles.title: Governor asks for status report on all public universities in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement. The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated.

Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State.

“Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said.
The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka.

articles.title: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff after GOP’s midterm defeat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: On his social media site, Donald Trump praised Susie Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation

President Donald Trump said Friday (November 6, 2026) that Stephen Miller was replacing Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff, mere days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections.
On his social media site, Mr. Trump praised Ms. Wiles and said she’d continue working for his political organisation. Ms. Wiles also released a social media statement on Friday (November 6, 2026).

"Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honour of a lifetime. I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together, from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First,” Wiles said in a social media post shortly after Trump’s announcement. She added that her commitment to “the President and the mission” will not change.
Mr. Miller, long a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a key architect of the administration’s hard-line immigration policies.
Ms. Wiles, the steely political operator and longtime adviser to Mr. Trump, was the first woman to ever serve in that post.
Ms. Wiles' departure comes almost immediately after the GOP's midterm thrashing on Tuesday (November 3, 2026). She will be replaced by Stephen Miller, a longtime trusted aide to Mr. Trump.

The departure also came months after Ms. Wiles indicated she no longer showed evidence of breast cancer after she underwent months of treatment for the disease, a diagnosis she went public with in March 2026.
Ms. Wiles is the longest-serving White House chief of staff for Mr. Trump, who cycled through four of them during his first four-year term.

Mr. Miller is one of Mr. Trump’s closest and longest-serving advisers, having jumped on board during his long-shot 2016 presidential campaign as a speechwriter. He currently serves as White House deputy chief of staff, and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, Mr. Miller is most closely aligned with Mr. Trump’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration.
Mr. Miller is a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

articles.title: West Bengal election is not legally valid: Former CEC S.Y. Quraishi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The former top poll official also reinstated that the Election Commission of India is supposed to make decisions based on a majority

Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi alleged that the West Bengal elections were not legally valid. He reinstated that the decisions at the Election Commission of India should be based on a majority.

“Were the West Bengal elections legally valid? In my opinion, it was not. I have said this several times; I will say it again. Now it is in front of the Supreme Court; I am hoping they will take the right decision,” Mr. Quraishi said. He further added that some parts of it may have been valid but also said that in places where there was suspicious of majority Muslim voters being removed must be rechecked and go for re-polls if needed.

“This government has been in power for 6-7 months. People are happy. But some people are raising questions, maybe because they did not get the outcome that they desired,” Minister Dilip Ghosh said on Friday (November 6, 2026), reacting to Mr. Quraishi’s allegations. He also warned that accepting the people’s verdict and choice of government is the right decision; otherwise the people opposing it have a “tough” road ahead.

This comes after the former CEC raised allegations against the SIR process and discrepancies at the West Bengal elections while delivering the keynote address at the Hashim Abdul Halim Memorial Lecture on Thursday (November 5, 2026) in Kolkata.

“The CEC is not the Election Commission. The rules first call for unanimous decisions. If that is not possible, there must be a majority-based decision among the three members of the ECI,” Mr. Quraishi said. He added that the CEC is not the ECI on their own, and their decision alone cannot be final.

The former CEC said this in reference to The Indian Express report, which had claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 objections to the various decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Meanwhile, Mr. Quraishi also said that the voter is not supposed to beg for their voting rights; rather, tradition in the past ensured that voter cards were delivered to the homes of each voter, and they did not have to negotiate to be included in the voter lists. He accused the special intensive revision (SIR) was used as a process to do backdoor checks for citizenships.

“It was neither smooth nor transparent. So many questions were raised that are currently being heard in the Supreme Court. Now, things will come out clearly once their judgment arrives, regarding what went wrong and what was correct,” Mr. Quraishi added.

articles.title: Pakistan says willing to issue visa to Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann for visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 23, Bhagwant Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27 questioning whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan
Pakistan on Friday (November 6, 2026) said it would consider issuing a visa to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann if the Indian politician wished to visit the country.
Pakistan Foreign Office Spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan made the remarks during his weekly media briefing in response to a question about the possible visit of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader.

The Pakistani government would “consider issuing him a visa if he wished to visit the country”, Mr. Khan said, clarifying that whether the Indian government permits Mr. Mann to travel to Pakistan was an entirely separate matter.
On October 23, Mr. Mann had said that he had been invited to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore on November 27.
However, he questioned whether he would be allowed to travel to Pakistan. “Our culture is the same. Many poets from here will go there,” he had said.
Mr. Mann had also expressed his desire that all legislators of the Punjab Legislative Assembly visit Kartarpur Sahib in Pakistan if the Kartarpur Corridor reopened.

The corridor, which connects Dera Baba Nanak in India's Punjab with the historic Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan, was established to facilitate Sikh pilgrims travelling to the shrine associated with Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism.
It allows Indian pilgrims to visit the gurdwara without requiring a visa for Pakistan, subject to the applicable arrangements.

The corridor has remained closed to pilgrim movement from the Indian side since May 7, 2025, when India launched pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following the Pahalgam terror attack.
Pakistan said it remained ready to facilitate pilgrims once the restrictions were lifted.
The foreign office spokesperson said Pakistan welcomes pilgrims of all faiths and remains committed to facilitating visits to religious sites.

He said the country issued more than 9,000 visas to Indian religious pilgrims in 2025, including Sikh and Hindu pilgrims, and issued over 4,000 additional visas to Sikh pilgrims during the first half of this year.

articles.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects

Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people.

articles.title: A missing persons complaint that unravelled Bengaluru’s seven murders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered.

It was not until the mother of Nalini, one of the seven allegedly killed by cab driver-turned-YouTuber Indushekhar, lodged a missing person complaint that the police found the first clue to the murders. While the murders allegedly took place between October 16 and October 31, the last two bodies were disposed of on November 1 or 2.

Senior police officers said that Sunita, the accused’s wife, and Roopavathi, his mother-in-law, were the first to be murdered. Sunita and Indushekhar had been married for 20 years, and an officer said they had been having regular arguments throughout their marriage. Sunita worked as a typist for an advocate, while Indushekhar was a cab driver. Their respective jobs were often a point of contention between them.
“Indushekhar claimed that he was verbally abused and harassed by his wife and her family, while her brothers also encouraged her to fight with him,” a senior officer said.
Prima facie , the police have found that Indushekhar had been planning the murders for over a year. The growing friction and pent-up anger allegedly came to a head following a recent meeting.

“The accused claimed that Roopavathi had visited his house on October 14, when she and Sunita reportedly verbally abused him. This became a trigger point, and he wanted to eliminate them,” the officer said.

According to the police, Sunita and Roopavathi were murdered first. Subsequently, the accused invited Sunita’s younger brother Shivakumar and his wife Divya to his house on the pretext of hosting a dinner party. The couple were then killed along with their seven-year-old son Puneeth. On October 30, the accused allegedly invited Shankar, another brother of Sunita, and his wife Nalini, and allegedly murdered them.

On November 3, Tungamma, Nalini’s mother, approached the police, stating that her daughter’s phone was switched off and that their house in Srirampura was also locked. Tungamma subsequently went to Indushekar’s house to check on him but found that his house was locked as well.

Sensing that something was amiss, she contacted Divya’s mother Kalavathi, who also said that her daughter and son-in-law were missing. Tungamma then lodged a missing person complaint with the Srirampura police.

Karthik, a shopkeeper near Indushekhar’s house, said a police team visited the house on November 3 and made inquiries about Indushekhar among the neighbourhood residents. “They also came the next day and questioned people because Indushekhar’s house was locked,” he said.

A senior officer told The Hindu that the police grew suspicious and began tracking Indushekhar. Several technical inputs indicated that he was on the move. “Finally, when he was in the city, we tracked him and intercepted his car,” he said.

High drama unfolded near the Rajajinagar police station on Friday as Nalini’s family accused the police of delaying action on their complaint. “We approached the police on November 1 itself, but they did not register our complaint. Only after two days did they take it up,” a family member alleged.
Bengaluru City Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh refuted the allegations and said that action would be taken against the officers if any lapses were found.

articles.title: Epic failures: on electoral roll, welfare
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The electoral roll cannot be used to determine welfare beneficiaries

Union Panchayati Raj Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s statement that voter identity cards, with biometric authentication, will replace Aadhaar as the basis for identifying beneficiaries and making payments under his Ministry’s schemes runs contrary to existing laws and regulations. Essentially, the electoral roll, prepared in several States through the flawed Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI), will become the dataset to vet the identities of beneficiaries. This contradicts the Supreme Court’s May 27 judgment on the Bihar SIR and its observations while hearing petitions against West Bengal’s orders removing people deleted during the SIR from the Public Distribution System and the Annapurna Yojana. The Court held that the ECI may undertake only a “limited enquiry” into citizenship to decide who belongs on the electoral roll, and that “any action taken pursuant thereto is confined to electoral consequences alone”. The consequence of deletion from the rolls, it said, is “correspondingly limited” to a person’s place on the roll and their right to vote. The Court also called the EPIC “a derivative document, issued on the basis of inclusion in the electoral roll”, and held that relying on it to verify that very roll would defeat the exercise. It is ironic that Mr. Singh now wants this “derivative document” to be the determinant of welfare benefits.

Not every citizen is an eligible voter, and tying benefits to the electoral roll is illogical and also cruel. In West Bengal, lakhs were deleted from the rolls , many for dubious “logical discrepancies”. In the appeals heard for reinstatement, 93% resulted in the restoration of names by September 2026, pointing to massive pre-election disenfranchisement. The Court has stated that it is yet to adjudicate on the legality of the ECI’s “logical discrepancies” method. The SIR was designed by the ECI to restrict enrolment through stringent residency criteria; thus, itinerant voters had to prove their eligibility. The Opposition, civil society and even some of the BJP’s allies have objected to this, but the BJP refuses to acknowledge the SIR’s flaws. This is partly because it has benefited from disenfranchisement — as in West Bengal. But the Minister’s remarks suggest another reason. The BJP-led coalition sees the pruned electoral rolls as a way to limit welfare, especially at a time when growth in tax revenues has slowed because of the Centre’s policies. Inordinately delaying the Census, changing the procedure to appoint Election Commissioners, who then run an exercise that disenfranchises millions by design, and now, using the resultant rolls to decide who gets welfare, all cut at the heart of the painstakingly built constitutional welfare state. The sooner the Court decides the petitions against the SIR, and reiterates that its rolls cannot be used to curtail welfare, the better.

The death toll in the explosion at an Oil India Limited (OIL) facility in eastern Assam’s Dibrugarh rose to two after one of six persons injured in Friday’s (November 6, 2026) fire died at a private hospital on Saturday (November 7, 2026) morning.
Reportedly working for a Mumbai-based private agency engaged by the oil exploration major, 40-year-old Tapas Gogoi died at around 3 a.m., taking the death toll in the fire incident to two.
The other person, identified as Raju Dutta, died from the impact of the explosion on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning.
The fire broke out at around 9.05 a.m. at the indirect bath heater in OIL’s intermediate tank farm at Tengakhat. The bath heater was isolated on November 4 for maintenance.

articles.title: Bus overturns as driver falls asleep, seven injured in Tirupati
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The driver has reportedly dozed off and applied sudden brake while the bus slipped towards an adjacent canal, which was not clear due to stagnant rainwater on the road

At least seven passengers were injured after a private bus met with an accident on the National Highway (NH-140) near Ithepalle village in Chandragiri mandal of Tirupati district on the early hours of Saturday (November 7, 2026).

According to the police, the bus belonging to Sri Naveen Travels was proceeding from Bengaluru in neighbouring Karnataka to Bhubaneshwar in Odisha, when it overturned opposite a Bharat Petroleum bunk around 4.30 am.

As per the preliminary information, the driver has reportedly dozed off and applied sudden brake while the bus slipped towards an adjacent canal, which was not clear due to stagnant rainwater on the road.

The injured passengers, including the driver, were admitted into Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS) Hospital in Tirupati. The remaining 34 passengers were sent to their destinations in another bus.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt sanctions ₹198 crore as honorarium for officials involved in 2026 Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Government order, issued by the Public (Elections) Department, stated one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officials and staff members involved in 2026 Assembly election

The Tamil Nadu Government has accorded sanction for the release of ₹198 crore towards payment of honorarium to officials and staff members who worked for the conduct of the 2026 Assembly election across all 234 Assembly constituencies in the State.

A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Public (Elections) Department. Accordingly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹45,000, whichever is less, will be paid to District Election Officers (DEOs), Returning Officers and Assistant Returning Officers of Assembly constituencies, District Revenue Officers (Elections), Personal Assistants (Elections) to Collectors, Special Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations, District Revenue Officers (DROs), Deputy Tahsildars (Elections), Zonal Officers and Liaison Officers for Observers.

Similarly, one month’s basic pay, subject to a maximum of ₹30,000, whichever is less, will be paid to officers and staff working in the election wings of the offices of DEOs, DROs, Tahsildars, Commissioners of Corporations and Municipalities. The same arrangement will apply to members of Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Video Viewing Teams, Accounting Teams, Model Code of Conduct Teams, Assistant Expenditure Observers, Static Surveillance Teams and Zonal Assistants.
Other categories of staff have also been sanctioned honorarium under various slabs. This honorarium would be paid to the officers and staff members through DEOs concerned, the order said.

articles.title: CM Vijay orders ₹2,000-crore allocation to implement Vetri Laptop Scheme for college students
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Under the scheme, students pursuing first- and second-year undergraduate and diploma courses in government and government-aided colleges during the 2026-2027 academic year will be eligible for laptops

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) ordered the sanctioning of ₹2,000 crore to implement the Vetri Laptop Scheme with the objective to enhance the technological skills of college students.
According to an official release, the administrative sanction has been accorded by the State government to implement the scheme, which was announced in the Budget 2026-27, at a cost of ₹ 2,000 crore.

A High-Level Steering Committee, headed by the Chief Minister, will be constituted to monitor the implementation of the scheme. The Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu (ELCOT) has been granted administrative sanction to procure laptops and ensure quality control.

Under the scheme, students pursuing first- and second-year undergraduate and diploma courses in government and government-aided colleges during the 2026-2027 academic year will be eligible for laptops. The beneficiaries include students pursuing arts and science, engineering, polytechnic, ITI, medicine, veterinary sciences, fisheries, agriculture and law courses.

In addition, third- and fourth-year students pursuing professional courses in government and government-aided colleges who did not benefit from the laptop scheme during the 2025-26 academic year will also be covered. Considering the technological requirements of engineering students, they will be provided with laptops equipped with Intel Core i5 processors or equivalent specifications, the release added.

articles.title: Ex-Keralam Excise Commissioner flags corruption, bribery in report to govt; CPI(M) alleges Minister’s involvement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In report submitted to State government shortly before being relieved from the post, Seeram Sambasiva Rao mentions that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions

Former Keralam Excise Commissioner Seeram Sambasiva Rao, shortly before being relieved from the post , had submitted a report to the State government alleging corruption and collection of bribes by two senior officials of the Excise Department, officials said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Mr. Rao, who was serving as Excise Commissioner and Special Secretary in the Electronics and Information Technology Department, was transferred and posted as Special Secretary in the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Development Department.
In the report submitted to the government on Friday, Mr. Rao also mentioned that Excise Minister M. Liju was acquainted with one of the bar owners allegedly involved in the transactions.

According to the report, S. Vinod, who served as Joint Excise Commissioner (JEC), allegedly maintained close links with the owner of a bar in Muvattupuzha and acted as a liaison for the establishment in matters related to its licence.

An informant had alleged that Mr. Vinod demanded a monthly payment of ₹30,000 from the bar owner and had also received ₹50,000 for securing approvals related to bar timings and licence extensions, the report claimed.
The report also flagged allegations against Alappuzha Deputy Commissioner Ajay.
According to the information received by Mr. Rao, the owner of a bar at Kattachira in Kayamkulam was allegedly asked to pay ₹30,000 during the deputy commissioner’s inspection visits, it said.
The report identified the bar owner as Ratheesh and stated that he was known to the Excise Minister.
It also mentioned an alleged payment of ₹20,000 after Onam this year in connection with the renewal of the bar’s licence in April.
Mr. Rao recommended that Mr. Vinod and Mr. Ajay be immediately removed from field postings and transferred to offices such as the Excise Crime Records Bureau or Toddy Board.

He also recommended a Vigilance inquiry into the allegations of bribe collection, monthly payments and disproportionate assets against the two officials under relevant provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The report further called for stricter controls on posting officials facing allegations of financial irregularities to sensitive locations and establishments, and recommended that future transfers and appointments at the JEC, Additional Excise Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner levels be considered based on reports from the Excise Commissioner.

articles.title: OMCs refute Karnataka’s E20 report, seeks additional details about procedure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The state-owned OMCs held the 56 samples tested by them from across the state reported an average 19.3% ethanol content in the vehicular fuel.

Refuting observations about ethanol blend in petrol being as high as 31% in Karnataka, the three state-owned oil-marketing companies (OMCs) stated the tests were not conducted in accordance with prescribed statutory and technical procedure.

Citing discrepancies with findings from their own quality monitoring, they urged the State government to share the complete counterpart sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports, and details about the adopted testing methodology, and samples for retesting.

“The OMCs remain committed to cooperating with the state government and other competent authorities in conducting joint sampling and testing in accordance with the Control Order and the Marketing Discipline Guidelines, 2024,” it stated, adding, “Any deviation established through the prescribed procedure will be dealt with in accordance with applicable guidelines.”
The OMCs raised concerns about the Karnataka Dept of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology’s use of the gas chromatography for evaluating ethanol concentration.
The process broadly entails separating compounds via vaporisation.

According to the OMCs, the certificates cited for the State government’s observations do not specify the applicable standard test method, the procedure for diluting the compounds or the reference material used for correction after vaporisation.
“In the absence of these essential details, the reported ethanol figures of 26-31% cannot be independently validated against the methodology prescribed under IS 17021,” the statement read.

Further, pointing to the Karnataka government’s reported observations, it observed, “Given that ethanol has a higher density than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the density of the blend. This discrepancy [in Karnataka’s reported samples] further underscores the need for testing through the prescribed methodology and verification against appropriate reference samples.”
The three OMCs put forth that 56 samples from across the State tested by them conformed to the prescribed specifications, reporting ethanol content between at an average 19.3%.
Thus, arguing that the “substantially higher ethanol levels” reported by the State Dept. warrant a “transparent, technically sound and jointly verifiable testing exercise.”

On similar lines, putting forth concerns about the Karnataka State Dept’s observations on 10% mileage loss and the ensuing ₹62,000 crore loss to consumers, it called for a transparent assessment of actual vehicle performance data, material compatibility studies and documented repair costs.

articles.title: Amid price rise, Centre mandates rice, paddy stock declaration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: To prevent hoarding, Union government allows five southern States to impose stock limits

With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding.

Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy.
Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement.
Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders.

The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said.

To improve availability, the Centre is allocating additional rice stocks to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar for sale as Bharat Rice, and has asked them to explore all possible distribution channels, especially in the southern States.

The Centre has also doubled the target for rice sales through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) for 2026-27 from 25 lakh tonnes to 50 lakh tonnes. Around 25 lakh tonnes had been sold to private parties by October 31, compared to 11 lakh tonnes in the same period of the last year.
Trade and industry experts said deficient and uneven rainfall had contributed to rice inflation, particularly in premium non-Basmati varieties, and pushed up paddy prices in several markets.
Retail rice inflation rose to 8.25% year-on-year in September from 5.89% in August, with the average retail price at around ₹48.23 per kg, about 12% higher than a year earlier.
Experts, however, said the situation was not a nationwide crisis.
With government rice stocks at comfortable levels, they said, pressure was sharpest in regions and grades where supplies were tight.

articles.title: Top U.S., China officials raise trade 'concerns' as APEC approaches
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year

Top officials from Washington and Beijing held "frank" talks on their countries' testy trade relationship on Friday (November 6, 2026), ahead of an Asia-Pacific summit in China this month where their leaders are due to meet.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and discussed economic and trade commitments over the last year, both sides said.

The Americans stressed "the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments" and highlighted "concerns about recent Chinese actions", according to a statement released by the U.S. Treasury Department.

Mr. Lifeng, meanwhile, expressed "serious concerns over recent economic and trade restrictive measures imposed by the United States", according to a State media report shared online by Beijing's Commerce Ministry on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
The report did not specify which measures Mr. Lifeng was referring to, but added that the talks were "frank, in-depth and constructive".
Mr. Bessent "underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China's implementation of the arrangement", said the Treasury.

The statement referenced China's commitments from an October 2025 meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Busan, South Korea, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
China is hosting this year's APEC gathering from November 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, which could also see a trilateral meeting with Mr. Trump, Mr. Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry said this week it was in contact with Washington and Moscow about the possibility.

The Busan agreement, which reflected calming tensions between the superpowers after they had exchanged tariff escalations earlier in 2025, required China to purchase U.S. soybeans this year and through 2028.
China also agreed to suspend new export controls on rare earths and to issue general licences for exports of the materials.
The accord initially covered one year, but the two sides extended the ceasefire through to January 10, 2027, during Mr. Jinping’s September visit to the White House.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The accord initially covered one year, but the two sides extended the ceasefire through to January 10, 2027, during Mr. Jinping’s September visit to the White House.

articles.title: Iran says forces 'stronger' than at beginning of war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Republic’s armed forces, having gained experience from direct confrontation with United States and Israel, are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war, Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a U.S. State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including "facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," U.S. Central Command said on X .
The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

articles.title: United States offers $20 million reward for information on 'Iran's nuclear program': CENTCOM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. State Department program, Rewards for Justice, gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward

Washington is offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program, the U.S. Military said Friday (November 6, 2026), as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.

A U.S. State Department program, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," U.S. Central Command said on X .
The program was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran's "lack of compliance with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.
It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.
Mr. Trump has repeatedly said U.S. forces have effectively obliterated Iran's nuclear program.

"If we didn't hit Iran, you wouldn't have Israel today," Mr. Trump said Friday (November 6, 2026) night in West Palm Beach, Florida. "If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East."
But the President also said Iran, which he stressed has had its economy and Military severely damaged over eight months of war, is eager to end the conflict.
"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.
Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.
And on Tuesday (November 6, 2026) Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his Government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Earlier this week Mr. Trump said he still had to "take care" of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

articles.title: Secret Service arrests man near White House after he said he heard voices telling him to kill Trump
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill the Republican President

The U.S. Secret Service said a suspect has been taken into custody and charged after officers found him in a vehicle near the White House with multiple guns, claiming he heard voices in his head telling him to kill President Donald Trump .
The arrest Thursday night (November 7, 2026) happened after Secret Service officers approached a man "acting suspicious" in a parked car, according to a Homeland Security statement.
U.S. officials say the suspect, Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos, then went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation's capital and kill the Republican President.
Shortly after, officers discovered the suspect's vehicle had been reported stolen and he had three different firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition.

This is the latest in a series of arrests the Secret Service and other law enforcement agencies have made against individuals who have threatened Trump or his family members' lives since he returned to office last year.

The statement described Chrinos as a migrant from Venezuela who is in the country illegally after entering the U.S. through Texas in March 2024. DHS said he has been charged and currently remains in U.S. Marshals Service custody.
The White House did not provide comment, instead referring to DHS and USSS.

"Thanks to our brave Secret Service officers, this illegal alien with three firearms in his vehicle was arrested near the White House before he could harm anyone," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in the statement.

articles.title: Jay Rockefeller, heir to famed dynasty and healthcare advocate in U.S. Senate, dies at 89
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Jay Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families, who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of ​the Iraq War, died on Friday (November 6, 2026) at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.
His family did not provide a cause, the ‌newspaper added.

Mr. Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his ​five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as Governor of the poor coal-mining State.

Mr. Rockefeller voted ⁠in 2002 in favour of the Republican Bush’s measure authorising the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Mr. Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”
He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John ‌D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.
New York-born Jay Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ‌impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, ‌fight ⁠poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping ⁠the programme created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps States provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Mr. Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the 1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Mr. Obama’s measure, Mr. Rockefeller unsuccessfully ​sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance ‌program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Mr. Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would ‌not seek a sixth Senate term.

Before the Iraq invasion, Mr. Bush’s administration built the case for war by touting intelligence indicating ​Iraq owned an arsenal of weapons of mass destruction — they actually did not exist — and alleged ties between Iraqi leaders and the al Qaeda network responsible for the September 11, 2001, attacks on the U.S.
“If I had known ⁠then what I know now, I would have voted against it,” Mr. Rockefeller told the Charleston Gazette newspaper in 2004, referring to the 2002 war authorization measure.

articles.title: U.S. military carries out fresh targeted strikes on Iran as Tehran weighs mediator's proposals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five,’ says U.S. President Trump
President Donald Trump said the U.S. military on Friday (November 6, 2026) carried out new limited strikes on Iran, targeting an Iranian air defence system.
Iran state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the crucial waterway for oil shipments.
Mr. Trump in an exchange with reporters described the military action as "minor".

"They knocked out — they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device — and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Mr. Trump told reporters shortly after arriving in West Palm Beach, Florida, on Friday (November 6) evening.

Mr. Trump did not offer further details about the target. U.S. officials have reported that most of Iran's air defence systems were destroyed or severely degraded during a June 2025 bombardment by Israel and in the early stages of the current conflict. U.S. officials have assessed that Iran would try to rebuild them and other military infrastructure over time.

The U.S. military also reported carrying out what it described as defensive strikes on Monday (November 2). Explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
Friday's (November 7) strikes are the first since Mr. Trump's Republican Party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday's (November 3) midterm elections in the U.S.

The electoral setback was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Mr. Trump's execution of the conflict and elevated fuel prices, a byproduct of the war that's affected nearly every sector of the global economy.
In the days since Republicans' shellacking at the polls, Mr. Trump has vacillated between threatening to "destroy" Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.

Earlier on Friday (November 6), officials from the two West Asian governments said Iran is reviewing proposals presented by chief mediator Qatar aimed at addressing differences with the U.S. about Tehran's nuclear programme.

But one of the officials stressed that Iran, at least at the moment, remains unwilling to engage in negotiations with the Trump administration over its atomic activities until the U.S. agrees to several core conditions that Iran has been demanding be part of any ceasefire agreement.
The difference over Iran's nuclear programme is the thorniest issue and one that Mr. Trump insists must be resolved as part of any deal meant to end the more than eight-month-old war.

articles.title: The Siang dam and a threatened homeland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Adi community has been protesting against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh, saying it threatens their land, livelihoods, and civilisation. The agitation has turned violent in response to increasing use of force by the State authorities. The community alleges that the State government has used deceit, force, and threats to get consent for the feasibility study. Abhinay Lakshman reports on the resistance

A few kilometres from the entrance to Arunachal Pradesh’s Parong village, an unpaved road winds all the way down to the Siang river. At dusk, all that is visible at the beginning of the dirt road is the glint of freshly painted yellow barricades of the State police and the shine from the silver of the concertina wires that connect the barricades. The Central security forces who guard the check post here have two purposes — to respond to “unrest” and to stop anyone without “clearance” from proceeding to Siang’s waters.

Parong, in Siang district, is one of the three proposed sites identified by the State government for a Pre-Feasibility Report (PFR) to begin work on the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), developed by the National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC).

articles.title: Keralam Child Development Centre gets ₹35-lakh grant to study autism-related parental grief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Three-year project will examine chronic sorrow and coping mechanisms in ASD families.

The Child Development Centre (CDC), Thiruvananthapuram, has received an Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)-approved grant of ₹35 lakh for a three-year research project titled “Development and Validation of a Tool for Assessing Grief among Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.”
The project, led by CDC director Deepa Bhaskaran, aims to develop and validate a culturally relevant tool to assess grief among parents of children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).

“The study will use focus group discussions and in-depth interviews involving parents of children with ASD, bereaved parents, professionals working with children with ASD, and members of the general population to understand the dimensions and cultural expressions of grief in the Indian context,” Dr. Bhaskaran said.

According to her, parents commonly experience shock, denial, fear, guilt, anger, sadness, and helplessness following their child’s diagnosis. The grief, described as chronic sorrow or non-finite grief, can recur at different stages of the child’s development, particularly when expected developmental milestones are not attained.

“The findings will help facilitate the identification of grief-related concerns among parents and support the development of appropriate grief counselling protocols and support group interventions, ultimately contributing to improved psychosocial well-being among families of children with ASD,” she said.
Inadequate social support compounds parental distress, she noted.

“There is a need for healthcare professionals to recognise and assess parents’ emotional well-being alongside the rehabilitation needs of children with autism. Early diagnosis, psychological support, and training for professionals to identify grief and help families develop coping strategies are vital,” she added.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 07 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Keralam Child Development Centre gets ₹35-lakh grant to study autism-related parental grief

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Three-year project will examine chronic sorrow and coping mechanisms in ASD families.

The Child Development Centre (CDC), Thiruvananthapuram, has received an Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)-approved grant of ₹35 lakh for a three-year research project titled “Development and Validation of a Tool for Assessing Grief among Parents of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.”

The project, led by CDC director Deepa Bhaskaran, aims to develop and validate a culturally relevant tool to assess grief among parents of children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD).

“The study will use focus group discussions and in-depth interviews involving parents of children with ASD, bereaved parents, professionals working with children with ASD, and members of the general population to understand the dimensions and cultural expressions of grief in the Indian context,” Dr. Bhaskaran said.

According to her, parents commonly experience shock, denial, fear, guilt, anger, sadness, and helplessness following their child’s diagnosis. The grief, described as chronic sorrow or non-finite grief, can recur at different stages of the child’s development, particularly when expected developmental milestones are not attained.

“The findings will help facilitate the identification of grief-related concerns among parents and support the development of appropriate grief counselling protocols and support group interventions, ultimately contributing to improved psychosocial well-being among families of children with ASD,” she said.

Inadequate social support compounds parental distress, she noted.

“There is a need for healthcare professionals to recognise and assess parents’ emotional well-being alongside the rehabilitation needs of children with autism. Early diagnosis, psychological support, and training for professionals to identify grief and help families develop coping strategies are vital,” she added.

fullParagraphs: The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index.

Hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana also expressed concern over “bumper-to-bumper” traffic in Delhi-NCR.
“We keep talking and sometimes make statements and suggestions, but the point is that AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI said.
The Bench highlighted the large number of vehicles plying on roads connecting Delhi with neighbouring areas, including Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad.
“Look at the roads in Delhi and the roads connecting Delhi with the NCR. Take a look at any road and the kind of vehicles moving on it. That is the major problem,” the CJI said.
The Bench said the poor people are the real sufferers, as they are on the roads, and moreover, the festival time is the only period when they earn a livelihood.

On stubble burning, the Bench stressed the need to educate farmers about using machines instead of resorting to farm fires.

On the plea seeking closure of schools or running them in hybrid mode for students of all age groups if the air quality index (AQI) rises above a certain mark, the bench said it will go by experts’ opinion.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, referred to the regulatory framework covering five major sectors: industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, construction and demolition dust, road dust and stubble burning.

articles.title: Kochi doctor booked for sexual assault a day after actors’ arrest on his complaint

A 41-year-old doctor was booked by the Infopark police on Friday (November 6, 2026) for the alleged sexual assault of a woman, a day after three people, including two actors, were arrested for allegedly assaulting and robbing him.
The case was registered against Dr. Johnson Varghese on a complaint filed by a relative of one of the accused in the case.

The alleged incident took place between 6.30 p.m. and 10.30 p.m. on November 2, 2026.

articles.title: OpenAI to press ahead with data-centre expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth

OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-centre expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fuelled fears of tighter scrutiny ​of the facilities, its Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar told CNBC in an interview on Friday.

“When ‌I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how ​do we keep investing to meet customer demand,” Friar said. “We are ⁠going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can get the compute we need,” she added.

One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly ‌to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry’s growth. It launched a charm offensive on Thursday to win ‌over communities as opposition to data centres becomes a rallying point for anxieties ‌about ⁠the technology.

As part of the efforts, OpenAI said, it will no ⁠longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites. It will also give residents access to construction plans and their potential effects.

Growing data-centre opposition was a crucial issue in the midterm ​elections. Democratic candidates, including Texas Governor-elect Gina ‌Hinojosa, made tighter scrutiny of the facilities a central campaign pledge. The Lone Star State is one of the fastest-growing data-center regions in the world.

Fears the Democratic sweep may slow construction of the facilities critical to the AI boom ‌wiped about $2.5 trillion off the US stock market on Thursday, as investors ​weighed the fallout for the chip, cloud and networking industries that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the spending frenzy.
Still, there are ⁠signs that tech giants remain committed to data-centre expansion plans despite the growing backlash.
Alphabet-owned Google said on Thursday it would invest $17 billion to build its first data centre ‌in Wyoming.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance is considering expanding a data centre project in northeastern Brazil, a move that would strengthen its standing as Latin America’s leading builder of computing facilities.
Friar also told CNBC that OpenAI was raising fresh capital, pushing back against suggestions the ChatGPT maker had scaled back its fundraising ambitions amid the sharp AI stocks selloff.
The company is seeking fresh capital after ‌its business grew 70% quarter over quarter in the third quarter, with enterprise demand doubling over the ​same period, she said.
“It (the growth) is saying people are actually using AI and getting value from it,” Friar said.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh MPTC, ZPTC election results LIVE: TDP leads in multiple Zilla, Mandal Parishads
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha and other top officials are monitoring the counting.
A media person collapsed after suffering a heart attack while covering election updates at the Narsipatnam counting centre in Anakapalli district.
The journalist was identified as Chintakayala Giri, a representative for Andhra Jyothy from Nathavaram mandal.
The incident caused panic on the premises as medical emergency services were unavailable, highlighting a concerning lack of basic ambulance facilities at the key official venue.

Decision will be taken soon on conducting elections to 23 municipalities, State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha said. He said that elections to these Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) could not be held with the other 100 ULBs that went to polls on November 1, due to administrative and legal issues.

The counting of votes for the MPTC and ZPTC elections is proceeding smoothly in a peaceful atmosphere at the counting centers, with no untoward incidents reported so far, said District Collector Dr. S. Venkateswar.
He along with SP L. Subbarayudu addressed the media here on Saturday.

He said that the counting started by 8 a.m. and the results for 55 to 60 MPTCs across the district have been completed. The counting process for the remaining MPTCs is being expedited, and it is expected that the results for all MPTC seats in the district will be announced by 2 p.m. and those of ZPTC seats by 6 p.m.

Results of the MPTCs started to trickle in from Kurnool district and they went in favour of ruling TDP. TDP’s Lakshmanna has won as the MPTC of Erragudi in Krishnagiri mandal, Gummala Keerthi of TDP won as MPTC in M Kottala of Aluru mandal, and H Padma won as the MPTC of Dibbanakal in Adoni mandal.
TDP is leading in 14 out of 20 ZPTCs where counting of postal ballots was completed. There are 27 ZPTCs in Vizianagaram district. Counting is going on in another seven places.
Both TDP and YSRCP are hopeful of victory in Kotia group of villages of Salur mandal of Parvatipuram Manyam district where poll percentage is around 35%.
This, in spite of strong objection from Odisha over conduct of local body elections in those villages located at the AP-Odisha border.

The counting of votes for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections began peacefully across Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district on Saturday, with the district administration making elaborate arrangements to ensure a smooth and transparent process.

articles.title: CPI(M) seeks anti-BJP alliance in Tripura civic polls to avoid vote split
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CPI(M) has fielded 263 candidates across 345 wards, while the Congress has nominated candidates in 221 wards after seat-sharing talks between the two INDIA bloc partners failed

CPI(M) Tripura State Secretary Jitendra Chaudhury on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said the party was keen to forge an electoral understanding with democratic and secular parties to prevent a split in anti-BJP votes in the civic elections.
His statement came a day after the deadline for filing nominations for elections to 21 civic bodies, including the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC), ended.
The CPI(M) has fielded 263 candidates across 345 wards, while the Congress has nominated candidates in 221 wards after seat-sharing talks between the two INDIA bloc partners failed.

"The date for filing nominations for the civic elections ended yesterday, and scrutiny has begun. We are still hopeful of a seat adjustment with anti-BJP parties, as defeating the saffron party is our main political objective," Mr. Chaudhury told reporters.

Accusing the BJP of weakening democratic values in Tripura over the past nine years, the Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly said he had held discussions with the leadership of a major anti-BJP party on an electoral understanding.

"We emphasised seat adjustment with anti-BJP parties to avoid a split in the anti-BJP vote bank in the civic elections. articles.title: Wayanad landslides: Despite township progress, 13 Adivasi families still caught between ‘no-go zones’ and delayed rehab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Some now live in rented accommodation with government assistance, cut off from their forest environment and traditional livelihoods. Others have returned to the forest, as construction of the promised houses on alternative land allocated to them at Puthiyavillage in Meppadi under Forest Rights Act, 2006 is yet to begin

Even as the rehabilitation of survivors of the 2024 Wayanad landslide (Mundakkai-Chooralmala landslide) in Keralam is making progress, with 327 families, including 149 last month, having been allotted houses at the township project in Kalpetta, the resettlement and rebuilding of lives remain a distant prospect for 13 Adivasi families displaced in the aftermath of the disaster.

Though their homes were not damaged, the families had to leave as the areas surrounding their settlements fell within designated ‘no-go zones’ (unsuitable for habitation), with one of the settlements also falling in a ‘red zone’. Some now live in rented accommodation with government assistance, cut off from their forest environment and traditional livelihoods. Others have returned to the forest, as construction of the promised houses on alternative land allocated to them at Puthiyavillage in Meppadi under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is yet to begin.

articles.title: Abhishek alleges attack by ‘BJP hooligans’ on residence, claims 7th attempt on his life in 6 months
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Trinamool MP alleged that his residence was attacked by ‘BJP hooligans’ on the occasion of his birth anniversary
Mamata All India Trinamool Congress leader and Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that his residence was attacked by “BJP hooligans”.
Mr. Banerjee shared the video of the attack on his social media handle and said that this was the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months.
Kolkata Police enforces prohibitory orders under Section 163 of BNSS outside Mr. Banerjee’s residence in Kolkata Kalighat area

“After two days of continuous recce, this is how BJP hooligans attacked my house at 2 AM today. Watch the footage and see for yourself... This is the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months. Yet, there has been no police action and no judicial intervention,” the Trinamool leader posted on social media.
Mr. Banerjee said that “if this is what can happen to an elected Member of Parliament, imagine the plight of the common man in West Bengal”.

After two days of continuous recce, this is how BJP hooligans attacked my house at 2 AM today. Watch the footage and see for yourself. If this is what can happen to an elected Member of Parliament, imagine the plight of the common man in WB. This is the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months. Yet, there has been no police action and no judicial intervention. Hooligans are running riot across the state because the judiciary continues to turn a blind eye. Thank you, Milords, for remaining mute spectators! 🙏🏻

On the occasion of his birth anniversary on Saturday (November 7, 2026), his supporters gathered in front of his house in the Kalighat area. A group of BJP supporters appeared and started shouting slogans, “thief, thief”. Photographs of the Trinamool leader, cutouts and banners hung with birthday wishes were torn. When Trinamool supporters tried to stop this, an argument started between the two camps, and clashes broke out.
Mr. Banerjee came out of his house and met his supporters, some of whom had sustained injuries. “There is a conspiracy to attack me and kill me,” he alleged.

In the video shared by Mr. Banerjee on social media, a mob is seen attacking the house with sticks and tearing banners on shops next to the house. A few police personnel in uniform are seen pushing away the mob.
The Trinamool leader also added that “hooligans are running riot across the State because the judiciary continues to turn a blind eye”.

“Thank you, Milords, for remaining mute spectators!” he said. Earlier, on Thursday (November 5, 2026) evening, the nephew of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee had said that the Trinamool lost elections to the Supreme Court and not to the Bharatiya Janata Party.

AITC chairperson and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee criticised the attack. “Who gave them the right to attack someone’s house at 3 AM? Who authorised such an attack? We have come here to lodge our complaints against the harassment, intimidation, and deliberate obstruction occurring in our locality. Even basic work in the neighbourhood is being disrupted, and people are being prevented from carrying out their religious celebrations peaceful,” she said to reporters outsider her residence in Kalighat.

articles.title: Faith meets fitness: The Keralam church where prayers come with pull-ups
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, has set up an open gym to promote fitness among parishioners. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.

Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.

The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.

“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.

When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.

“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.

The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.

The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.

For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.

The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.

For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

articles.title: Congress Govt lifted more water from Godavari than the BRS government: Govt Whip Aadi Srinivas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Harish Rao getting vicarious pleasure in drought conditions: Aadi Srinivas

Countering the BRS criticism that Godavari water was released to Andhra Pradesh, Government Whip Aadi Srinivas said the Congress government had lifted more water from the Godavari than the BRS government.

Presenting the figures at a press conference in Hyderabad on Saturday (November 7, 2026), he said the previous BRS government had lifted a total of 86.127 TMC of water through the Devadula project between 2014-15 and 2022-23, averaging 9.57 TMC annually.

In comparison, the Congress government had lifted around 68 TMC in the last three years, he claimed. It lifted 18.067 TMC in 2024-25 and 18.20 TMC in 2025-26, averaging 18.13 TMC annually, which was 89% higher than the average during the previous regime, he said. The government had already lifted 16.71 TMC during the first five months of the current year, he added.
