fullParagraphs: New Zealand’s election remained too close to call on November 7, as early results trickled in from across the country, with neither the governing National-Luxon coalition nor Labour falling short of a majority and minor parties weighing in, including a rising Opportunity Party

The outcome of New Zealand's election remained too close to call as early results began to roll in on Saturday (November 7, 2026), with none of the parties expected to secure a majority after a campaign dominated by worries over rising costs of living and the economy.
Kiwis are struggling to make ends meet — the price of basic goods remains stubbornly high, and unemployment is at its highest in more than a decade.
The war in West Asia and the subsequent global fuel shock have been widely blamed for the hit to New Zealand's trade-dependent economy.

Prime Minister Christopher Luxon hoped his right-wing coalition could cling to power with promises of no new taxes, after three fractious years in office, two failed bids by his own National Party to oust him as leader and an economy in the doldrums.
Former Premier Chris Hipkins' centre-left Labour have promised help with living costs, from free doctor's visits and prescriptions to a cap on public transport fares.
He said on Friday (November 6) he was sure his party would "exceed expectations".
At a Labour event in Upper Hutt near Wellington bedecked with red balloons, party workers were quietly confident they had secured the largest number of seats.
And at a National gathering in the country's largest city of Auckland, cheers rose from the crowd as the party's candidates were shown to be ahead.
Police minister and National lawmaker Mark Mitchell told journalists it was "very close".
"When you reflect on what's happening globally, we certainly see lots of geopolitical uncertainty," he said.
"I think considering that we've governed through that period, we're actually doing quite well."
By 9:00 p.m., with over 30% of the votes already counted, the two main parties were neck-and-neck, with National on 41 projected seats and Labour on 36, data from the electoral commission showed.

articles.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, first Muslim U.S. Senator-elect?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan’s open U.S. Senate seat on Tuesday (November 4, 2026), according to media projections, becoming the first Muslim elected to the chamber and preserving a crucial Democratic seat in the party’s fight for Senate control.

His victory denied Republicans the chance to fill the seat left vacant by retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. The 42-year-old former public health official ran on a progressive platform focused ⁠on lowering costs for working families and ⁠reducing corporate influence in politics.
His win marked a breakthrough for the Democratic Party’s progressive wing ‌in this closely contested midterm election cycle.

Abdul El-Sayed was born on October 31 , 1984, in Rochester Hills, Michigan, U.S.. He attended public schools, where he captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams. He was raised by his father, Mohamed, an Egyptian immigrant and his stepmom, Jackie, whose family has lived in Gratiot County, Michigan since the 1800s. Mr. El-Sayed earned his undergraduate degree with the highest distinction from the University of Michigan where he also played on the Wolverine men’s lacrosse team. He went on to earn a medical degree from Columbia University under an NIH-funded fellowship, as well as a second doctorate from Oxford University as Rhodes Scholer.
He lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku and their two daughters.

Although trained as a physician, Mr. El-Sayed shifted his focus to public service after realising the political systemic issues that was deteriorating public health, according to his campaign website.

He rebuilt Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy and led Wayne County’s Department of Health. Human & Veterans Services, serving 1.8 million residents. His public service spans several achievements, including securing free eyeglasses for children, targeting major environmental polluters, making the life-saving Narcan universally accessible and pioneering a programme projected to cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 3,00,000 Michiganders, as per the website.

He authored Medicare for All: A Citizen’s Guide and served on former President Biden’s 2020 Unity Task Force for Healthcare to help develop policies aimed at lowering prescription drug costs. His public service earned him recognition as “Public Official of the Year” by the Michigan LCV and also a spot on Crain’s Detroit Business 40 Under 40 list.

Mr. El-Sayed won the U.S. Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. He launched his campaign to lower living costs and ensure government agencies serve working people rather than billionaires.

Mr. Rogers, 63, ‌a former Congressman and FBI agent, entered ​the race with strong backing from President Trump and national Republicans and sought ⁠to cast Mr. El-Sayed as a radical candidate sympathetic to Islamic extremism through alleged ties to the Muslim ‌Brotherhood, claims that Mr. El-Sayed denies and that remain unsupported by evidence. Democrats said the attacks on Mr. El-Sayed relied on Islamophobic tropes, according to Reuters.

Mr. Rogers also devoted significant effort to courting Jewish voters who may have been uneasy with Mr. El-Sayed’s opposition to U.S. military ‌aid for Israel and his characterisation of Israel’s actions in ​Gaza as genocide.

But Mr. Rogers struggled to overcome voter concerns about the economy and ⁠President Trump’s low ratings. In the closing weeks of ⁠the race, he broke with the President on the war in Iran and the ‌U.S. trade dispute with Canada, arguing that ending both was necessary to help bring down costs ​for businesses and consumers.

articles.title: U.S. midterm election results: Senate, House and Governor shifts before and after
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Democrats surged to full control of Congress in the November 2026 U.S. midterm elections, flipping the Senate and House after winning net seats across key battlegrounds and sweeping into Republican strongholds. Here’s what changed between 2022 and 2026 midterms.

The November U.S. midterm elections saw a major shift in Washington’s power dynamic as Democrats captured full control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress, by crossing the 218-seat threshold needed for a majority.

In contrast to the 2022 midterms, where former President Joe Biden’s Democrats defied expected losses by holding the Senate and narrowly losing the House, the 2026 midterms saw Democrats gain full control of both chambers of Congress.

The almost dramatic swing towards Democrats, by the very same voters in the conservative bastion that propelled President Donald Trump to a second term just two years ago, is a result of widespread discontent over economic pressures including high living costs along with foreign policy decisions regarding the war with Iran. Voters elected Democratic candidates across the conservative strongholds and swing states creating a divided government under Mr. Trump.

In the 2022 midterms, pre-election predictions pointed toward a powerful “red wave” favouring Republicans due to surging inflation and low approval ratings for Mr. Biden. But the wave failed to fully materialise. Democrats defied the trends by retaining control of the Senate (reaching 50 seats after picking up Pennsylvania and holding Nevada), though Republicans narrowly flipped control of the House of Representatives with a slim majority.
In the 2026 midterms, the story was different. Democrats scored a sweeping victory over the ruling party, seizing control of both Senate and the House of Representatives.
In 2022 midterm elections, Democrats entered the election with a 50-50 split (with Vice-President Kamala Harris as the tiebreaker) and expanded their narrow control.

They gained a net seat by flipping Pennsylvania (where Democrat John Fetterman defeated Mehmet Oz) and secured a majority by holding Nevada (Catherine Cortez Masto), finishing with 50 seats to Republicans’ 49.

In 2026, Democrats captured full control of the 100-seat upper chamber by making historic inroads into Republican strongholds. The Democratic Caucus has currently secured 54 seats to achieve majority after defending its existing seats and winning key races, while the Republican Caucus has secured 44 seats. The counting is still under way.

Major wins include James Talarico gaining a Senate seat in Texas, Kansas electing its first Democratic Senator since the Great Depression and Democrats defeating Mr. Trump’s handpicked candidate in South Carolina (Democrat Annie Andrews ousting Republican Darline Graham).

In 2022, Republicans gained control of the House, gaining nine net seats to secure a narrow majority of 222 seats compared to the Democrats’ 213 seats, crossing the majority mark of 218 seats in the 435-seat chamber. This narrow margin of victory was potentially close to the 221–212 margin seen in 2001.

Meanwhile, in 2026, Democrats reversed those gains in a nationwide rout. Democrats have officially won 239 seats, surpassing the 218 needed for a majority. Republicans have secured 147 seats. The final counts are still being finalised.

Gubernatorial contests saw Democrats pick up two net Governor’s mansions in 2022, maintaining 24 governorships to the Republicans’ 26. Before the election, Republicans held a 28 to 22 seat advantage. Also, voters in 2022 rejected election-denier candidates in battleground State races for Governor, Secretary of State and Attorney General (with 12 out of 13 such candidates losing).

articles.title: U.S. FBI and regulators issue warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial refrigerators
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The U.S. regulators warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems,” shortly after these hacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarkets
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and government regulators on Thursday (November 5, 2026) issued a warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial coolers and fridges.
The warning acknowledged that hackers were targeting vulnerabilities in unpatched or internet-linked refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.
Gaining control of these systems would enable hackers to adjust temperatures to dangerous extremes or run unauthorised defrost cycles, leading to the spoilage of inventory or even fire hazards.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT) warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.”

The U.S. FBI-issued factsheet recommended that organisations with cold storage facilities de-link control system devices from the internet, enhance password security, apply patches to keep systems updated, and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates.

The notice came shortly after cyber attacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarket franchises, where some fridge temperatures were raised as high as 50 degrees Celsius in October.
Food and produce had to be thrown out at a mass scale, along with large quantities of melted ice.
The perpetrators behind the attacks have not yet been identified or apprehended.

“Industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems protect food, medicine, and other temperature-sensitive products, making them attractive targets for malicious cyber actors. We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” said FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman.

articles.title: A sub-adult elephant found dead in Shankara Range in Shivamogga
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials suspect the animal was electrocuted after coming into contact with a live electric wire along the edge of a paddy field
A sub-adult male elephant, aged about 10 to 12 years, was found dead at Ichavadi village in the Shankara Range of Shivamogga Division on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
Officials suspect the animal was electrocuted after coming into contact with a live electric wire along the edge of a paddy field.

Officers from the Shankara Range and Shivamogga Division visited the spot. During the preliminary inquiry, they questioned Alimiya, a resident of the village, according to a press communique issued by the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Shivamogga Division.

The suspect told the officers that he had erected a fence and connected it to a power supply to protect his ripening paddy crop from wild boar. A case has been registered under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

The Forest Department has also asked MESCOM officials to initiate action against the accused under the Electricity Act. The statement added that the carcass will be disposed of in accordance with the standard operating procedure.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi interview: ‘Great damage done to the fabric of India by BJP’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ahead of the launch of her book, Sonia Gandhi speaks to The Hindu, answering a number of questions — personal and political

In this wide-ranging interview to The Hindu on her soon-to-be-launched book, Belonging: A Journey of Love , published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi responds in writing to a number of questions, personal, historical, and political, raised by N. Ram.

The subjects covered include how she came to write her story about belonging; the values she grew up with and came to learn and cherish in India; what she learnt from Rajiv Gandhi and Indira Gandhi and how they shaped her life and outlook; the “great damage … done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions” by the BJP-RSS dispensation; how she viewed, and now looks back on, the Emergency of 1975-1977; the major political decisions she made to accept the office of Congress President in 1998 and to continue in it, after a challenge by some colleagues, in 1999, and in 2004 to decline the offer to become Prime Minister; the current political situation and the prospects of the Congress and its coalition partners; and the change of publisher in India just weeks before the book’s launch.

‘Others have spent decades telling my “story”,’ you posted on X the other day, ‘now it’s my turn.’ My AI-assisted bibliographical search suggests there are at least 75 books, including several biographies, that attempt or purport to tell your story in substantial measure. Your post hints that you were amused rather than irritated or angry about others presuming to tell your story. Am I right? And did you read those books, or at least some of them, written by biographers and others who spent decades telling your ‘story’?

I had no idea there were so many! But I have never felt like reading books about myself. A long time ago Rajiv and I realised that there was no point in trying to keep up with all that had been written about us. But, as I say in the book, there came a time when I felt that I should tell my own story.

In the Prologue to Belonging , you give us an insight into how you came to write your story, ‘perhaps…a story worth sharing,’ as you put it somewhat self-deprecatingly. Was it the ‘chorus’, which was on your case for years, or something within you, or both that eventually pushed you over the line to give us this intimate and unusually candid story? And may I ask how long it took you to write the book, breaks and all?

It’s been such a long time that I’ve lost track, but it has certainly been more than a decade since I first wrote a bit. I only started writing in earnest about five years ago. It wasn’t an uninterrupted process. There were times when words and thoughts flowed, others when nothing would come out, and I would throw my hands up in frustration.

You describe Belonging as a personal memoir, with politics providing the background or ‘a kind of framework’. But it’s really a love story at its heart and that’s how I read it. The story of an extraordinary, instantly formed magnetic bond of love between Rajiv and Sonia, which gradually grew into something much larger, drawing you into the highest circles of power, then reluctantly into public life and politics, and eventually making you one of the country’s foremost political leaders. Stranger than fiction, isn’t it?

Yes! That’s one reason I had no desire to talk about it for so long. But it is not only a love story between the two of us, it’s also the story of how I grew to love Rajiv’s family and the country to which they belonged, and then I too came to belong in it. And of how this love brought me into public life, when I saw the purpose of all the sacrifices they had made being threatened, and the party was weakening. I felt I had to do something.

The writer R.K. Narayan once observed that, despite the passage of time and physical ageing, ‘the chap inside is the same,’ capturing the enduring sense of self. You grew up in a small town in Italy, in a family and social environment far removed from the world that you would eventually inhabit and make your own. Looking back over more than six decades in India, how much of that young Italian woman survives in the person you are today?

The values that I learnt growing up survive. I have tried my best to be true to them: loyalty to family and friends, sincerity and feeling for others, the idea of being dutiful and responsible. I think I can say that in these I am the same person Rajiv met sixty years ago. But I used to smile and laugh a lot more then!

Rajiv Gandhi, the love of your life, and Indira Gandhi, with whom you shared an exceptionally close bond, are central figures in your story. Looking back, what do you see as their defining qualities and the ways in which each shaped your life and outlook?

When I arrived in India as a young bride, I knew nothing about India. All that I am and know today, I learnt from them. Their courage, their empathy, their commitment to a secular and democratic India and most of all, the pull of duty that was greater than any other for both of them was something that inspired me and held me steadfast during times of difficulty and doubt.

articles.title: Voter ID for welfare? What Rajiv Ranjan Singh’s proposal could mean | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Opposition parties have linked this announcement to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, in which 13.5 crore electors were reportedly removed. They argue that disenfranchisement will now be coupled with exclusion from welfare programmes.

Story so far: Union Minister for Panchayati Raj and senior JD(U) leader Rajiv Ranjan Singh, alias Lalan Singh, on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) said that voter cards, along with biometric authentication, will be the basis for identifying beneficiaries and processing payments for welfare schemes. He argued that Aadhaar cards can be easily made at every street corner, implying that they can lead to fraudulent beneficiaries. He presented the use of voter cards along with biometric authentication as a possible mechanism to deal with such cases.

The ration card was the first mass-scale identity document, introduced during colonial rule just a few years before the eclipse of the Empire. Welfare entitlements came to be linked to stable residences and enumerated households. It was the first time that both a residential address and a household were formally enumerated, giving a singular identity to the Indian family.

articles.title: Congress pushing Telangana towards ‘Asset bankruptcy’, alleges BJP leader Gudur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress government is pushing Telangana towards “asset bankruptcy” by relying on auctions of valuable government lands to meet its immediate revenue requirements, alleged senior BJP leader Gudur Narayana Reddy.

In a statement made at Hyderabad, he warned that continued disposal of public assets could weaken the State’s financial credibility, constrain its future borrowing capacity and affect its ability to finance welfare schemes and infrastructure projects.

Citing CAG-related figures, Mr. Narayana Reddy said Telangana received ₹16,478 crore from land, property, and miscellaneous sources in 2023-24, accounting for about 69% of its non-tax revenue. He said the erstwhile TSIIC had 53,473.76 acres as of March 31, 2022, and had made 2,355 land allotments covering around 4,050 acres between 2014-15 and 2021-22.

He pointed out that the BRS government had auctioned about 31 acres in the Raidurg-Knowledge City corridor for nearly ₹730 crore, while land prices at Kokapet Neopolis had touched ₹100.75 crore per acre in August 2023.

The BJP leader alleged that the Congress government had intensified the process since coming to power. He claimed that since January 2024, the Congress government had auctioned nearly 40 acres in Raidurg-Knowledge City for about ₹7,000 crore, at an average of ₹179 crore per acre. He also cited auction prices of ₹177 crore per acre in October 2025, ₹237 crore in May 2026 and ₹264 crore and ₹269 crore in August 2026.
Similarly, the three-phase HMDA auctions at Kokapet Neopolis in 2025 had fetched around ₹3,708 crore for 27 acres, averaging ₹137 crore per acre, he said.

Referring to HMDA’s proposal to auction another 114 land parcels with an estimated revenue target of ₹2,000 crore, he questioned the rationale behind continuing to depend on land sales for revenue mobilisation.
He also expressed concern about the implications for future industrial development, noting that, as of September 2025, TGIIC reportedly had 5,730 acres available for industrial allotment.

articles.title: Siang dam protesters released in Arunachal Pradesh after nearly month in detention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014

Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh were released from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday (November 7, 2026), nearly a month after their arrest, officials said.
The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they added.

Their release came a day after the State Government agreed to free them as a goodwill gesture while responding to demands raised by the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF), which has been leading the protest against the proposed mega dam.
The development marks a significant step towards easing tensions in the Siang Valley, where opposition to the project has triggered protests and confrontations in recent months.

In a letter dated November 6, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) also approved the reinstatement of suspended gaonburas and gaonburis affected by disciplinary action in connection with the SUMP agitation.
The Government, however, maintained that the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters would have to follow due legal process.

It also said the demand for withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel from the region would be discussed during the proposed meeting with SIFF representatives, taking into account the prevailing security situation.
The Government has urged SIFF to resume dialogue and communicate a convenient date, along with a list of delegates, for a proposed meeting with Chief Minister Pema Khandu.
It also appealed to the organisation to encourage residents of Siang and Upper Siang districts to maintain peace and refrain from violence, intimidation and attacks.

The CMO's communication, signed by Shibu Thomas, Principal Private Secretary to the Chief Minister, reiterated the government's commitment to addressing the concerns of the Adi community through a mutually acceptable roadmap.
The release of the four protesters was among SIFF's key demands before agreeing to participate in talks with the government.
The forum had earlier rejected Mr. Khandu's invitation for dialogue, insisting that its demands, including the release of detainees and withdrawal of security forces, be addressed first.

articles.title: Under-construction roof of school auditorium collapses in Keralam; no casualties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred around noon at PKS Higher Secondary School, Kanjiramkulam, near Neyyattinkara. The roofing work was carried out on Friday, but heavy rain later affected the structure, officials said
An under-construction roof of an auditorium at an aided school in Keralam collapsed on Saturday (November 7, 2026). However, no one was injured, officials said.
The incident occurred around noon at PKS Higher Secondary School, Kanjiramkulam, near Neyyattinkara, Education department officials said.
The auditorium had a tin-sheet roof, and work was underway to replace it with a concrete structure.
The roofing work was carried out on Friday, but heavy rain later affected the structure, officials said.
The entire concrete roof structure, including the steel bars and supporting poles, collapsed, they said.
As it was not a working day, there were no students on the premises.
The workers present at the site managed to move to safety after noticing the roof collapsing, officials said.
Work has begun to clear the debris, and Public Works Department officials will examine whether any defects in the construction work led to the collapse, officials added.

articles.title: Vance distancing himself from Trump ahead of 2028 Presidential race: Ex-U.S. NSA Bolton
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Bolton described Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Trump's tariff policies

U.S. Vice President J. D. Vance is trying to distance himself from President Donald Trump by blaming the Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war as he prepares for a potential 2028 Presidential bid, former U.S. national security adviser John Bolton has said.

In an interview with PTI Videos , Mr. Bolton described Mr. Vance's remarks as "very wrong" and a "big political mistake", saying the Republicans overlooked broader voter dissatisfaction with the economy, rising prices, and Mr. Trump's tariff policies.

"There's no doubt that part of the underlying reason for Mr. Vance’s statement was that this is the beginning of his 2028 nomination campaign. And he's trying something very politically risky here," he said.
Mr. Bolton argued that the Iran war was only one factor behind voter discontent, pointing out that Mr. Trump's tariffs had contributed to persistently high prices.
He said Mr. Trump had promised during the 2024 Presidential campaign to address economic concerns better than the Biden administration, but had failed to deliver after taking office.

"The voters took him at his word. They said we have more faith that Mr. Trump can handle these issues than Mr. Biden and Ms. Harris. So he gets elected, he comes in, and he doesn't do it. And if anything, he's causing more problems," the former U.S. NSA said.

Mr. Bolton also emphasised how the Iran war pushed up international oil and gas prices and increased energy costs for American consumers. "What they opposed was the higher price of gasoline. And Mr. Trump didn't even attempt to address that," he added.

He described the Democrats' strong midterm performance as a "stinging repudiation" of Mr. Trump, saying voters across party lines were tired of his leadership, though the results did not necessarily amount to an endorsement of the blue team.
He also said Mr. Trump was unlikely to fundamentally change his leadership style during the remaining two years of his term, despite the electoral setback.
"Trump's whole operating style for 10 years is: I don't work with anybody. I represent the people, and I'm going to do what I want to do," Mr. Bolton stated.
He further warned that a Democratic-controlled Congress could launch investigations into the Trump administration, including allegations of corruption, self-dealing and self-enrichment.

On U.S.-India ties, Mr. Bolton said domestic political turmoil in Washington could push foreign policy priorities to the sidelines, affecting discussions on defence cooperation and common security challenges in the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Who is Stephen Miller, Trump’s new Chief of Staff?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Stephen Miller, one of U.S. President Donald Trump’s closest aides for decades, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) named Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new Chief of Staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after Republicans were hammered in the midterms.

Ultra-loyalist Miller, 41, will replace Susie Wiles, who becomes the first major White House casualty from the Democratic landslide earlier this week . In a post on Truth Social announcing Mr. Miller’s appointment, Mr. Trump described him as “one of my most trusted advisors”.

Stephen Miller, a key member of Mr. Trump’s inner circle, is a prominent architect of the administration’s hardline immigration policies. Known for his sharp suits and sunglasses, Miller has been one of Mr. Trump’s closest aides for decades and longest-serving advisers, pushing nativist policies that gelled with the President’s “America First” agenda.

Mr. Miller currently serves as White House Deputy Chief of Staff and though he has a wide-ranging portfolio, he is most closely aligned with the President’s immigration policy and rhetoric on immigration. He is also a former aide to hardliner former Sen. Jeff Sessions, R-Ala., who would go on to serve as Mr. Trump’s first Attorney General.

Mr. Miller was raised in politically liberal Santa Monica, California, but developed a reputation as a combative conservative as a columnist at Duke University’s student newspaper. ⁠As a congressional aide in the 2010s, he was an early advocate for restricting immigration at a time when that was not a mainstream position in the Republican Party.

He joined Mr. Trump’s 2016 presidential campaign, then served ‌as an advisor and speechwriter in his first 2017-2021 term. After Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election, Mr. Miller founded the conservative advocacy group America First Legal, filing complaints that accused companies ‌such as Nike of discriminating against white people.
His wife, Katie Miller, is a conservative podcaster and former ⁠communications aide in Mr. Trump’s first administration.
As Mr. Trump’s Deputy Chief of Staff for policy and homeland security advisor, he was the brains behind the mass deportation programme that defined the first year of the President’s second term.

Mr. Miller is best known for driving the immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests per day — far above levels under previous administrations. He has pushed U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to target anybody in the country illegally, ‌not just those with criminal records.
But he faced widespread criticism after the deadly shootings of two protesters by immigration agents in Minneapolis in January — incidents that sparked mass demonstrations.

Beyond enforcement, Mr. Miller has been a vocal advocate for ending birthright citizenship, and denounced the ⁠Supreme Court’s ruling that rejected that proposal as “one of the most destructive and outrageous decisions” in the court’s history.
Mr. Miller announced a ban on “birth tourism” after that ruling, seeking to prevent people from coming to the ‌United States to deliver babies.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), rising tensions in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay, turned violent as hundreds of thousands stormed the streets to protest locking out of their accounts in the country’s biggest bank. As fires burned and people anxiously queued outside the collapsed bank, President Santiago Pena, a former shareholder in the bank, announced his resignation.

But as Congress moved to impeach him, Mr. Pena disappeared amid rumours that he had fled to Argentina — just as Brazilian far-right leader Flávio Bolsonaro did last week before fleeing to U.S. after losing the election to President Lula da Silva. “We have information that he left the country without telling anyone. I think he went to Argentina and sought asylum,” said Paraguayan Senator Antonio Velázquez on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

articles.title: The science behind sleep supplements - melatonin and magnesium
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Doctors warn that there is no replacement for natural solutions, and supplements cannot be taken over a long period

If a good night’s sleep has become your holy grail, who are the knights in shining armour you will employ to reach that chalice? Most people seem to be deploying melatonin and magnesium supplements, over the counter, but the question that remains is: are they effective, and if so, at what combinations or levels?

The consensus among most sleep specialists, is that both melatonin and magnesium (glycinate) can have an ameliorative impact – in the short term. Both these supplements, however, work differently – while melatonin is a key body clock signal, magnesium helps relax the body. When and how you take both supplements makes a great deal of difference to your hours of sleep and sleep quality as well.

articles.title: At COP31, the ‘overshoot’ narrative cannot replace climate action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: No COP decision has referred to the quantitative value of the total or remaining carbon budget nor has discussed which countries have spent it the most. If COP31 is to deliver real impetus to climate action, its decisions must revert to the basics

COP31 is around the corner, marking the end of a year of extreme weather events, terrible human tragedy, as well as a severe energy crisis. It is also the year in which the world is preparing to officially accept that we will exceed a warming level of 1.5 degrees celsius.

The natural corollary to this unassailable reality is that countries should strive to collectively limit warming to as little over 1.5 degrees celsius, and as below 2 degrees, as possible. This requires scientific discussions, assessment of options, and a critical analysis of the trade-offs. However, what we have instead is another buzz word: ‘overshoot’.

articles.title: T.N. CM Vijay writes to PM Modi expressing concerns over inspection of Union govt. officials regarding Mekedatu dam project
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: CM Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing his concerns regarding the site inspection conducted by the Union government officials in connection with the Karnataka government’s proposal to construct the Mekedatu dam.

He urged the Prime Minister that no statutory or administrative approvals be granted without the consent of the co-basin States, while emphasising the need to ensure the sustained water availability in the Cauvery basin of Tamil Nadu.
In his letter, Mr. Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka.

“The said proposal of Government of Karnataka to construct Mekedatu reservoir across Cauvery with a huge capacity of 67.16 TMC, just upstream of inter-State border between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, would not only prevent the flows due to Tamil Nadu but also prejudicially affect the monthly deliveries to the inhabitants of Cauvery Basin of Tamil Nadu, as stipulated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” Mr. Vijay said in his letter.

There have been frequent news reports on Karnataka Chief Minister’s meeting with the officials of Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for clearance of DPR of Mekedatu Project, without the concurrence of Tamil Nadu, which keep the farmers of the State in a state of perpetual anxiety , he said.

“Earlier, a team of officers of the Government of India reportedly visited the proposed Mekedatu Dam site, as per the statements emanating from the State of Karnataka. The anxious farmers of Tamil Nadu view the site visit as an indication of tacit movement on a project that would jeopardise their very livelihood. Such actions, the purported site inspection by Government of India officials, have deepened the worries of the farmers of Cauvery delta, who are already struggling in this deficit water year (2026–27), due to Karnataka’s denial to ensure Tamil Nadu’s due share even on a pro-rata basis,” Mr. Vijay said.

Mr. Vijay also referred to his earlier letter dated July 28, where in he requested the Prime Minister to ensure that no statutory or administrative approval be granted to the Mekedatu Project, unless it is demonstrably consistent with the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Judgment.

The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a unanimous Resolution on June 19, reiterating its demand on the proposed Mekedatu project and also filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court with a prayer to withdraw the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in December, 2025, on the preparation of DPR for irrigation and multi-purpose project proposals, exclusively for Cauvery basin, since the basin is held to be a deficit by the Tribunal in February, 2007. This matter is still pending in the Supreme Court of India, Mr. Vijay pointed out.

“It is vital that the rights of lower riparian States regarding both the quantum and regulated pattern of monthly releases remain fully protected and hence, consideration or examination of DPR of Mekedatu Project submitted by Karnataka or any unilateral technical evaluations or site inspections by central agencies at this juncture are highly inappropriate,” he said.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 07 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

T.N. CM Vijay writes to PM Modi expressing concerns over inspection of Union govt. officials regarding Mekedatu dam project

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

CM Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressing his concerns regarding the site inspection conducted by the Union government officials in connection with the Karnataka government’s proposal to construct the Mekedatu dam.

He urged the Prime Minister that no statutory or administrative approvals be granted without the consent of the co-basin States, while emphasising the need to ensure the sustained water availability in the Cauvery basin of Tamil Nadu.

In his letter, Mr. Vijay said there was an apprehension growing among farmers of Tamil Nadu over the recent developments with respect to the proposed Mekedatu Dam Project of Karnataka.

“The said proposal of Government of Karnataka to construct Mekedatu reservoir across Cauvery with a huge capacity of 67.16 TMC, just upstream of inter-State border between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, would not only prevent the flows due to Tamil Nadu but also prejudicially affect the monthly deliveries to the inhabitants of Cauvery Basin of Tamil Nadu, as stipulated by the Hon’ble Supreme Court,” Mr. Vijay said in his letter.

There have been frequent news reports on Karnataka Chief Minister’s meeting with the officials of Ministry of Jal Shakti (MoJS), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for clearance of DPR of Mekedatu Project, without the concurrence of Tamil Nadu, which keep the farmers of the State in a state of perpetual anxiety , he said.

“Earlier, a team of officers of the Government of India reportedly visited the proposed Mekedatu Dam site, as per the statements emanating from the State of Karnataka. The anxious farmers of Tamil Nadu view the site visit as an indication of tacit movement on a project that would jeopardise their very livelihood. Such actions, the purported site inspection by Government of India officials, have deepened the worries of the farmers of Cauvery delta, who are already struggling in this deficit water year (2026–27), due to Karnataka’s denial to ensure Tamil Nadu’s due share even on a pro-rata basis,” Mr. Vijay said.

Mr. Vijay also referred to his earlier letter dated July 28, where in he requested the Prime Minister to ensure that no statutory or administrative approval be granted to the Mekedatu Project, unless it is demonstrably consistent with the Final Award of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal (CWDT) and the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Judgment.

The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a unanimous Resolution on June 19, reiterating its demand on the proposed Mekedatu project and also filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court with a prayer to withdraw the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in December, 2025, on the preparation of DPR for irrigation and multi-purpose project proposals, exclusively for Cauvery basin, since the basin is held to be a deficit by the Tribunal in February, 2007. This matter is still pending in the Supreme Court of India, Mr. Vijay pointed out.

“It is vital that the rights of lower riparian States regarding both the quantum and regulated pattern of monthly releases remain fully protected and hence, consideration or examination of DPR of Mekedatu Project submitted by Karnataka or any unilateral technical evaluations or site inspections by central agencies at this juncture are highly inappropriate,” he said.

articles.title: A total of 28 illegal immigrants apprehended, expelled: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a post on X, Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity

“Police in Assam 's Sribhumi district apprehended and expelled 28 Bangladeshi nationals allegedly staying illegally in the State,” Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).
In a post on X, Mr. Sarma said the State government would continue its drive against infiltration and would not compromise on Assam's security and identity.

"Assam's patience with infiltration is over. Twenty-eight illegal migrants detected by Sribhumi Police were expelled. We will continue this mission with unwavering determination. No compromise on our borders. No compromise on the security and identity of Assam,'' he added.

Assam has an integrated checkpost in Sribhumi and a land customs station at Mankachar. Mr. Sarma had earlier said the State government is committed to an infiltration-free Assam. The Border Security Force has intensified its vigil along the 1,885 km Indo-Bangladesh border in the Northeast since the 2024 disturbances in Bangladesh. Assam Police has also maintained a high alert along the International Border to prevent illegal entry.

articles.title: Karnataka Police Complaints Authority member proposes seniority badges for police personnel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel

A member of the Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority, has urged the State Government to introduce special designations and insignia on police uniforms to recognise the seniority of personnel based on their years of service, irrespective of promotions.

In a letter dated November 5 to Minister for Home, IT-BT and E-Governance Priyank Kharge, Karnataka State Police Complaints’ Authority member Mohan Kumar Danappa proposed introducing three categories of seniority for police personnel, from constables to non-IPS officers.

According to his proposal, personnel completing five years of service should be designated as ‘Senior’, those completing 10 years as ‘Super Senior’, and those completing 15 years as ‘Most Senior’. He has suggested that distinct insignia corresponding to these designations be displayed on the right side of the chest, above the nameplate.

Mr. Danappa pointed out that although police personnel generally become eligible for promotion after five years of service, promotions are largely dependent on the availability of vacancies. As a result, many experienced personnel continue in the same rank for years without any formal recognition of their seniority and experience.
He said the proposed system would recognise their long service, enhance their sense of responsibility and ensure that experienced personnel receive due respect within the department and society.

Citing the practice of providing black collar patches to IPS officers after 10 years of service, he said similar arrangements were also followed in certain State police forces and Central Armed Police Forces.

He also referred to the State Government’s recent initiatives to replace British-era police caps and introduce lanyards in place of whistle chains, stating that recognising seniority through uniform insignia would be another significant reform to boost the morale of police personnel.
If implemented, Karnataka could become the first State in the country to introduce a structured system of seniority-based designations and uniform insignia for police personnel, he said.
Mr. Danappa has requested the Home Minister to examine the proposal and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities for its implementation.

articles.title: Bengaluru cab driver kills wife, six members of her family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The murders are believed to have been carried out between October 16 and November 3, with the bodies dumped at multiple locations on Bengaluru’s outskirts, including one near the foothills of Nandi Hills in Chickballapur.

In a shocking murder spree in Bengaluru , a 52-year-old man allegedly killed his wife and six members of her family, including a seven-year-old boy, and disposed of the bodies over a span of 18 days, police sources said. An 11-year-old boy, who is also a relative of the accused, has been rescued.

The accused was allegedly assisted by his 17-year-old college-going daughter, whose exact role is yet to be established. Family disputes are believed to have been the motive for the murders, although the police have not ruled out any other angle and are interrogating the accused.

The prime accused, identified as Indushekar, a cab driver and YouTuber who also ran a monthly tabloid, has been arrested by the Rajajinagar police. The murders are believed to have been committed between October 16 and 31, while the last two bodies were reportedly disposed of on November 1 and 2.

A preliminary police investigation revealed that the accused, with the help of his daughter, invited the relatives to his house on the pretext of a non-vegetarian dinner or a party. “After dinner, when the relatives fell asleep, the accused used a grinding stone to kill the victims. There is also a suspicion that he may have spiked their food. However, the police are awaiting medical reports to ascertain the cause of death,” a source said.

According to the FIR, which also records the accused’s statements, the bodies were dumped at multiple locations on the city’s outskirts and elsewhere in the State, including Yercaud Ghat, Chamundi Hills, Nandi Hills, and Shiradi Ghat. He allegedly used his sedan car, that he used as a cab, to dispose of the bodies. So far, the police have been able to trace only one body, that of the seven-year-old boy.

The incident came to light after a family member of one of the deceased lodged a missing complaint at the Srirampura police station. Subsequent investigations led to Indushekar being detained, and his statements unravelled a series of horrific murders that allegedly took place at his house near Bhashyam Circle in Rajajinagar, north Bengaluru.

The deceased have been identified as Indushekar’s wife, Sunita (40); his mother-in-law, Roopavathi (65); his two brothers-in-law, Shivakumar (30) and Shankar (44); their wives, Divya (30) and Nalini (29); and Shivakumar’s son, Puneeth (7).

An investigator in the case told The Hindu that the accused had maintained that his wife and mother-in-law did not respect him and frequently verbally abused him, while her family supported them. “The accused claims to have been planning the murders for many months. A recent visit by his mother-in-law did not go well, which angered him,” the source told The Hindu.

articles.title: Siang dam protesters released in Arunachal Pradesh after nearly a month in detention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014

Four protesters detained over the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh were released from Jully Central Jail near Itanagar on Saturday (November 7, 2026), nearly a month after their arrest, officials said.
The four, identified as Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained on October 9 under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014, they added.

Their release came a day after the State Government agreed to free them as a goodwill gesture while responding to demands raised by the Siang Indigenous Farmers' Forum (SIFF), which has been leading the protest against the proposed mega dam.
The development marks a significant step towards easing tensions in the Siang Valley, where opposition to the project has triggered protests and confrontations in recent months.

In a letter dated November 6, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) also approved the reinstatement of suspended gaonburas and gaonburis affected by disciplinary action in connection with the SUMP agitation.
The Government, however, maintained that the withdrawal of FIRs against protesters would have to follow due legal process.

It also said the demand for withdrawal of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel from the region would be discussed during the proposed meeting with SIFF representatives, taking into account the prevailing security situation.
The Government has urged SIFF to resume dialogue and communicate a convenient date, along with a list of delegates, for a proposed meeting with Chief Minister Pema Khandu.
It also appealed to the organisation to encourage residents of Siang and Upper Siang districts to maintain peace and refrain from violence, intimidation and attacks.

The CMO's communication, signed by Shibu Thomas, Principal Private Secretary to the Chief Minister, reiterated the government's commitment to addressing the concerns of the Adi community through a mutually acceptable roadmap.
The release of the four protesters was among SIFF's key demands before agreeing to participate in talks with the government.
The forum had earlier rejected Mr. Khandu's invitation for dialogue, insisting that its demands, including the release of detainees and withdrawal of security forces, be addressed first.

articles.title: Agents booked, five fertility centres named in Hyderabad’s illegal oocyte racket; Telangana Women’s Commission questions inaction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While cases have been registered against a few agents in connection with the alleged illegal collection of eggs (oocytes) from economically vulnerable women, the Telangana Women’s Commission has questioned why no legal action has been initiated against the hospitals and fertility centres allegedly involved in the racket.

The alleged exploitation came to light after 43 women were rescued during simultaneous raids in Hyderabad. Women from economically weaker sections were allegedly offered between ₹20,000 and ₹30,000 for an egg donation cycle, while those operating the racket reportedly made an average of about ₹3 lakh from each cycle.

Expressing strong displeasure over the delay, the Commission said that despite its directions to the concerned authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the hospitals and laboratories allegedly involved, no concrete steps had been taken against the institutions so far.

Ms. Nerella expressed concern over the fact that the whereabouts of Dr. Hussain remain unknown and that no case has been registered against him so far.

Questioning the delay in action, the Commission has urged senior officials of the health department to immediately conduct an inquiry into the allegations against the hospitals and IVF centres named by the affected women and initiate stringent legal action against those found responsible.

The Commission further warned that there would be serious consequences if there was any further delay in registering cases against those involved in unlawful activities concerning women’s bodily autonomy, dignity and health.

articles.title: Authoritarian leaders facing setbacks, says M.K. Muneer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chairperson of the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission M.K. Muneer urges the public to oppose hate speech irrespective of who makes it, asserting that there should be no compromise with those who spread hatred.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is destined to meet the fate of Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini, M.K. Muneer, chairperson of the Kerala Administrative Reforms Commission, has said. He was inaugurating the delegates’ meet organised as part of the Keralam State conference of the Muslim Youth League here on Saturday (November 7).

Mr. Muneer said the people are living in an era when authoritarian leaders are facing setbacks. “That is why Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu are being forced to confront resistance. They will ultimately meet the same fate as Hitler and Mussolini. Narendra Modi, too, faces a similar future,” he was quoted as saying in a release.
He urged the public to oppose hate speech irrespective of who makes it, asserting that there should be no compromise with those who spread hatred.

Shweta Bhatt, wife of former IPS officer Sanjiv Bhatt, who was the chief guest at the delegates’ meet, said that the legal battle and imprisonment of her husband have entered its eighth year, but the family will not retreat from its struggle for truth and justice.
She said that asking questions and defending constitutional rights were the true expressions of patriotism.
Muslim Youth League State president Panakkad Syed Munavvar Ali Shihab Thangal presided over the meeting. State general secretary P.K. Firos delivered the welcome address, said the release.

articles.title: NDA grabs 117 MPTC seats in Bapatla district, TDP wins 109

fullParagraphs: YSR Congress Party wins 19 MPTC seats; TDP emerges victorius in two ZPTC seats and is leading in four more

The ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), registered a decisive victory in the MPTC elections in Bapatla district by winning 117 seats of the 273 MPTCs taken up for counting of votes.

According to the updates received till the last report came in on Saturday, the TDP secured 109 MPTC seats, while its alliance partner JSP won eight. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) secured 19 seats, while others won one. The BJP did not register a victory in the results declared so far.

The TDP dominated several mandals, securing 17 seats in Martur, 12 in Parchur, 11 in Bhattiprolu, 10 in Repalle, nine in Chinaganjam, eight each in Karamchedu and Nagaram, seven in Yeddanapudi, six each in Cherukupalli and P.V. Palem, four in Nizampatnam, three in Bapatla, two each in Amruthalur and Tsundur, and one each in Chirala, Karlapalem, Kolluru and Vemuru.
The JSP won three seats in Repalle, two each in Cherukupalli and Karlapalem, and one each in Chinaganjam and the remaining mandal as reflected in the district tally, taking its total to eight.
The YSRCP secured 19 seats, including four in P.V. Palem, three in Parchur, two each in Bapatla, Chinaganjam, Karlapalem and Martur, and one each in Chirala, Karamchedu, Kolluru and Tsundur.
In the ZPTC elections, the TDP won two seats and was leading in four more. It emerged victorious in P.V. Palem and Yeddanapudi, while it was ahead in Bhattiprolu, Cherukupalli, Nagaram and Parchur.
The BJP and JSP had no ZPTC wins or leads, while the YSRCP also had no ZPTC victory or lead recorded in the tally.

articles.title: No respite from deluge even a week after rain: Residents of Palakol complain
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several colonies are in knee-deep water for the last few days, and there is no proper power supply and no supply of milk, vegetables and other essentials in some of the water logged areas, says the victims

With water still not receding even a week after Cyclone Murasu flooded the streets of Palakol in West Godavari district, residents see no help in sight as they complain that their efforts to raise the issue with authorities have gone in vain.

“The A.P. Housing Board Colony, Allu Venkata Satnarsyana Colony and the neighbouring areas were inundated. Flood entered many houses and damaged household articles,” said residents of Housing Board Colony.
As colonies were flooded, there has been no proper power supply, and streets remained inaccessible for milk and vegetable vendors, residents complained.
In some lanes, slush and garbage entered into the houses. Floodwater in the colonies has not receded, and snakes and poisonous reptiles were creating panic, said a resident, Vijaya Lakshmi.

“We have sent messages through social media groups to the Palakol Municipal and Revenue officials, and tried in vain to meet the public representatives. There has been no response from them,” said Sathi Babu of AVS Colony.

“Medicines and essentials are exhausted in several houses, and senior citizens, pregnant and lactating women were suffering, as the colonies are in knee-deep water,” Kumari, a resident whose house was damaged due to the cyclone, told The Hindu on Saturday.
A few people vacated as their houses were in floodwaters and went to safer places. There were no street lights too, Ms. Kumari added.

“When we visited the Sachivalayams, Revenue and Municipal offices, attenders and watchmen said the officers were on election duties. No steps have been taken to drain out the floodwater, a Kirana shop owner said.
“Flood water stagnated in low-lying areas, and many areas were water-logged for the last few days. We are trying to solve the problem,” an officer said.

fullParagraphs: Moscow has not commented on the incident. Russia has consistently ​denied any involvement ‌in cyberattacks or hacking operations abroad

Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Saturday (November 7, 2026) that his ​personal data had been published on the dark ‌web by what he said were ​pro-Russian hackers, adding that the ⁠move was linked to the Italian government's support for Ukraine.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who ‌has been one of the strongest backers of Ukraine among Western ‌leaders, expressed her support for Mr. Tajani and ‌said ⁠the sale of confidential information relating ⁠to public officials was "a matter of serious concern".
Moscow has not commented on the incident. Russia has consistently ​denied any involvement ‌in cyberattacks or hacking operations abroad.

Mr. Tajani, who is also Italy's deputy Prime Minister, said in a post on X ‌that "backing in a transparent way the ​freedom and independence of a sovereign state" had made him a ⁠target and that the hackers were seeking further information about him and his family and ‌were willing to pay for it.
The attacks were also a reaction to efforts by the Foreign Ministry to strengthen cybersecurity, Mr. Tajani added
Screenshots seen by Reuters showed Mr. Tajani's picture among a ‌list of 18 "citizens hostile to the Russian Federation", ​which also included cybersecurity experts

The material was found in a section ⁠of the dark web accessible through the Tor ⁠network as part of monitoring activities carried out by cybersecurity authorities, ‌a person close to the Minister told Reuters.
Further investigations are being undertaken, ​they added.

articles.title: Airstrike kills 22 people near Yemen's capital, Houthi official says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of November 7 strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital

Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday (November 7, 2026), killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.

Speaking to The Associated Press , Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.

The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a years-long truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis — who control Sanaa, the north, and the west of the country — and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.

On Friday (November 6, 2026), an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.

Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances, bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.
Mr. Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's (November 7, 2026) strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP .

In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance, capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

articles.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Islamic Republic’s armed forces, having gained experience from direct confrontation with United States and Israel, are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war, Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said

Iran said Saturday (November 7, 2026) its military has grown "stronger" since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran's nuclear programme.
Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the West Asia conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
Iranian Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.
He also said Iran's forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

"Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," he said.
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence."
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.
On Friday (November 6, 2026), the U.S. military said it was offering a $20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a U.S. State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including "facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," U.S. Central Command said on X .
The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Jana Sena Party (JSP) president and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan attributed the decisive mandate for the ruling coalition in the rural local body elections to the development and welfare measures undertaken by the government in villages.

articles.title: No complete closure of Ballari Road for 18 months for elevated corridor work: BDA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period.

The Hebbal Flyover and Ballari Road corridor will not be completely closed for 18 months to facilitate the construction of the elevated corridor, the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) clarified on Saturday (November 7). Meanwhile, the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) said vehicular movement would continue with limited lane restrictions and phased traffic diversions.

The clarification comes amid concerns over the traffic disruption expected during the construction period. The elevated corridor is part of the BDA’s larger Integrated Tunnel and Elevated Corridor Project, aimed at easing congestion along the city’s crucial northern corridor connecting Bengaluru with Kempegowda International Airport. However, the project has also drawn considerable public criticism since it was announced.

The BTP sources said restrictions would apply only to the movement of heavy vehicles between 6 a.m. and 8 p.m., while other motorists would merely be “advised” to take alternative routes. Public transport vehicles and school buses would also be allowed to use the stretch.

The BDA said barricading would be restricted to a lane approximately 4.5 metres wide, affecting only one of the three existing lanes in each direction. The remaining two lanes and the service road would remain open to traffic.

The concern, however, is that the 4.5-metre-wide lane is part of one of the main carriageways and accounts for 35% of the traffic movement on the stretch at any given time. Consequently, the restrictions are likely to worsen congestion, irrespective of the timing of their implementation. At least 20% of the traffic will therefore need to be diverted to prevent gridlock along the stretch.
“Even without civic works, the stretch witnesses prolonged congestion during peak hours. So, with civic works, the need for traffic diversion is essential,” a police source said.

This makes the advisory to use alternative routes necessary. However, the identified alternate routes are also in poor condition. The BTP has now written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and the BDA, requesting them to asphalt the alternative routes to ensure the smooth movement of vehicles and prevent congestion.

“Routes through New BEL Road and R.T. Nagar Station Road are among those being considered for improvement. Officials have also been asked to identify bottlenecks, improve road surfaces, and install adequate signage and road markings,” the BDA said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Routes through New BEL Road and R.T. Nagar Station Road are among those being considered for improvement. Officials have also been asked to identify bottlenecks, improve road surfaces, and install adequate signage and road markings,” the BDA said.

articles.title: 'Tough' stance on Kishau Dam project laid ground for victory in BBMB dues case: Himachal CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu says he had consistently raised the issue of dues arising from BBMB projects and made it clear to the Centre that the rights of Himachal Pradesh in the matter must be resolved before any further progress was made on the Kishau Dam project

Hailing the Supreme Court verdict in the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) arrears case, Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that the decision came in the State's favour on account of the "tough" stance his government took during discussions on the Kishau Dam project.

Mr. Sukhu said that during meetings with the Union Power Minister and officials, he had consistently raised the issue of dues arising from BBMB projects and made it clear that the rights of Himachal Pradesh in the matter must be resolved before any further progress was made on the Kishau Dam project.

He said the State asserted that it would not share the cost of the 440-MW Kishau Dam project, and the Haryana government assured that it would file an affidavit in the Supreme Court in favour of Himachal Pradesh for the release of arrears of its power share from BBMB projects.

Ruling in favour of Himachal Pradesh, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the hill State would get 11,973 MU of electricity from Punjab and Haryana over 20 years. The arrangement will be as per a 2011 Supreme Court verdict settling power dues arising out of Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydro projects since 1966 at the rate of 7.19%.

Talking to media persons here, Mr. Sukhu claimed that the case of arrears, pending for the past 15 years, would have taken many more years to decide if the government had not pursued it vigorously in the top court.

He said that the State government is exploring a better price to sell the electricity received from the BBMB. If the electricity is sold at the rate of ₹6 per unit, the State could earn around ₹500 crore, but the government is working towards securing a better power agreement that could increase the revenue to approximately ₹1,000 crore.

The Chief Minister said that the State government was moving ahead with the aim of making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant and expressed confidence that it would become the most prosperous State in the country by 2032.

articles.title: A woman stitches her way into the male-dominated ritual tradition of Theyyam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Based in Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur, she spends the Theyyam season creating attire and accessories, a craft she learned from her father and now sustains as a specialised, highly regarded artisan.

In the ritual world of Theyyam, where women rarely find a place in the traditional roles, 41-year-old M. Priya of Kannayi Mukkottu near Payyannur has carved out a distinctive space for herself. Rather than performing rituals, she stitches costumes and decorative garments that transforms male performers into divine figures in the Malabar’s sacred groves and temples.
For Priya, the Theyyam season is also the busiest time of the year. Beginning in November and continuing until March or May, depending on the festival calendar, it keeps her sewing machine busy.

Unlike conventional tailoring, Ms. Priya specialises exclusively in the traditional attire worn by Theyyam performers. She makes costumes and decorative accessories for almost all the Theyyam forms, following individual performances measurements and requirements.

“It takes nearly two days to stitch the complete costume for a Theyyam character. Each form has its own distinctive style of attire, requiring patience, precision, and an understanding of the traditional designs,” she said.

Ms. Priya’s learned the craft from her father, who stitched Theyyam costumes by hand before sewing machines became common. “I learned this by watching my father stitch the costumes at home. I developed an interest in this particular kind of stitching and gradually began doing it myself,” she said.

Although she has been involved in the work for over 15 years, Ms. Priya has never ventured into conventional tailoring. Performers from across Kannur and Kasargod districts approach her with their measurements and requirements.

Among the items she makes are kaani, kachunkaraa, Valinjery, kuttithaya and Velimban, Kayipodip, Thalachut besides several other components of Theyyam attire. Designs and stitching patterns vary according to the character, making each order a specialised assignment.

Orders pour in as the season approaches. Ms. Priya spends her evenings from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the sewing machine. Her work has earned the appreciation of performers who depend on the precision and quality of their costumes.
Prashanth Panicker, who has been performing Theyyam since very young age, has been getting his costumes stitched by Ms. Priya.

“Stitching Theyyam costumes requires a great deal of patience. Once we get the costumes stitched by her, there is hardly any need to look elsewhere. The stitching is precise. I perform in several places in Kannur and Kasaragod, and her workmanship has become a familiar signature in the costumes I wear,” he says.
For Priya, the craft is not merely an occupation. Theyyam runs deep in her family. Her father was associated with the tradition, while her brothers children too have performed theyyam.

Her husband M Sashi has been a constant source of encouragement. An auto-rickshaw driver, he supports her work, helps her find customers and pursue her interest. He drives more more actively when the Theyyam season winds down.
